2024:
In 2023, the data.gouv.fr team conducted an extensive survey on the impact of open data.

This survey is based on the French methodology for impact measurement and is inspired by European work, particularly the "Indicators for an Open Data Impact Assessment."

The study outlines the outputs, outcomes, and impacts for the four dimensions of impact (governmental, environmental, social, economic).

Regarding the outputs, a selection of indicators among those identified by the Commission were selected, including:
- Number of datasets on the theme
- Number of new datasets on the theme in 2023
- Number of views on these datasets in 2023
- Downloads of these datasets in 2023
- Number of discussions
- Number of reuses on the theme
- Number of new reuses on the theme in 2023
- Reuses by type
- Number of views on the reuses in 2023
- Discussions on the reuses

Regarding the outcomes and impacts, the use cases examined were selected from three main sources:
- The reuse catalog of the data.gouv.fr platform;
- The catalog of digital public services developed within beta.gouv.fr;
- The catalog of research publications on scanr.

And according to three criteria:
- High potential impact;
- Availability of resources and information;
- A balanced distribution in the four impact categories defined by the Open Data Maturity Report.

For each use case, a literature search was conducted and interviews were sometimes conducted with their designers to document the services, the data used, and the impacts created.

The results of this study will be published in 2024 in the form of six articles on data.gouv.fr and consolidated into a more comprehensive paper.

This is not the only study; we can notably mention the work of OpenDataFrance (DataImpact: new edition of the study on the reuse cases of environmental data - Open data france https://opendatafrance.fr/dataimpact-publication/) as well as the book by Dr. in Sociology Samuel Goëta “Les données de la démocratie: open data, pouvoirs et contre-pouvoirs” (https://cfeditions.com/donnees-democratie/) which provides a critical assessment of the impact of open data.

Impactful use cases on different impact areas have been identified, reviewed and researched, among which economic impact. On the theme of "innovation and adoption of new technologies," we focused on two use cases:

FireCaster

FireCaster is a research project, notably supported by CNRS, aiming to create a virtual reality fire simulation tool. It includes:

- An hourly weather fire index for forest fire risk prediction;
- A fire simulation based on a fire propagation model;
- A collaborative virtual reality platform.

These various layers have utilized public meteorological data (AROME data), as well as data on humidity and soil. The tool allows firefighters and decision-makers to better understand fire crises and manage them more effectively in real life.

L’indemnisation des dommages corporels confrontée au développement de l’IA et de l’open data

This research studied the application of open data from court decisions to the issue of bodily injury compensation. It establishes that the algorithmic analysis of these data, combined with human interpretation, presents an opportunity for more transparent and fair compensation for victims.

column13:
It is a simple yet effective from our experience methodology, that is initiated when a PSB is invited and agrees to publish its data on the national portal. The methodology includes the following steps:
a) Assignment of Open Data Liaison Officer by PSB
b) Open Data Liaison Officer undergoes the offered training programme (session open for PSB management on a voluntary basis)
c) PSB finalises its data publication plan with the assistance of a member of the Open Data Team (template, guidelines and support provided by the Open Data Team) 
d) PSB gradually publishes data on the National Open Data Portal according to its data publication plan
e) Open Data Team members monitor the progress by comparing each PSBs data publication plan against the datasets published on its National open data portal account and “pokes” the PSB if necessary.
f) PSBs are required to update and submit their data publication plans at least every 2 years (majority do it on an annual basis) – The Open Data Team reiterates the process described in (e)

column13:
The National Portal follows the DCAT-AP 1.0 framework. A slight variation, with more mandatory classes than the EU standard, as well as optional DCAT-AP fields. 
For practicality and for purposes of uniformity, two standardized usage licenses were chosen, specifically CC-BY 4.0 and CC BY-SA 4.0, from which public bodies can choose the most appropriate one during the process of publishing their datasets.

Minimum Metadata - Mandatory fields (15 fields):
Dataset Title, Description, Topics, Identifier (UUID), Groups/Organizations, License to Use, Language, Geospatial Coverage, Update Frequency, Start Date, Contact Link Name, Contact Link Email, Resource Title,Resource format, Access URL.

column13:
The methodology includes a number of actions such as:
(i) Desktop Research: Carried desktop research in order to identify new re-use cases in the form of applications and websites developed with the re-use of open data. The identified re-use cases are then published with the consent of the developer on the National Open Data Portal, in the section “Showcases”.     
URL: https://www.data.gov.cy/en/showcases

(ii) Open Data Portal Satisfaction Surveys: We have included a couple of questions on reasons of re-use in the 2018 Survey. We plan to incorporate additional questions in the next survey.

(iii) Monitoring the performance portal's indexes such as number of visitors, datasets' downloads, traffic through APIs and how these changed over time gives a proxy on the extend of re-use, especially in those areas where re-use does not take the form of applications.

(iv) Interaction and interviews of re-users of open data. 

(v) Commissioning Impact Studies at regular intervals in order to record visible and non-visible re-use cases and their impact.

Yes, The Data Governance Council in collaboration with stakeholders take decisions about any revisions or updates as required.  In fact Malta has during 2024 and Q1 2025 enacted a number of updates including:
- https://legislation.mt/eli/act/2025/6/eng : updates to the Re-Use of the Public Sector Information Act
- https://legislation.mt/eli/act/2024/19/eng: Amongst others empower MDIA for Data Intermediation and altruism Services and  matters related to the Data Governance Act and Data Act.
- https://legislation.mt/eli/ln/2025/20/eng - Organisational Structures for Data Sharing and Re-Use (Amendment) Regulations, 2025
- https://legislation.mt/eli/ln/2024/191/eng: Data Governance Regulations re: Data Governance Act.
The Public Administration Data Strategy 2023-2027 establishes a roadmap for Data Governance regulation, oversight and implementation through 39 actions.   The actions are reviewed from time to time to reflect evolving realities.  These actions are considered as performance indicators towards the strategy implementation.  The latest review (mid-term) was carried out in the 1st quarter of 2025 through the engagement of a company with the necessary expertise to take stock about the status of the actions’ implementation and the overall Data Governance Framework.  The Data Governance Council reviews any suggestions put forward, including suggestions that are collated through stakeholders and decisions are then taken about further updates and actions required.

The National Open Data Strategy 2024-2028 (including an Action Plan) was adopted by Government Decision on 12 December 2024. The Strategy was initiated by the Secretariat-General of the Government and was developed in a collaborative manner with relevant stakeholders (institutions and re-users) and is available here: https://legislatie.just.ro/Public/DetaliiDocumentAfis/293657; https://data.gov.ro/pages/cadrul-strategic. 1. Strengthening the open data governance framework
2. Animating the open data ecosystem
3. Publishing high-value datasets and ensuring the quality of published data
4. Encouraging data reuse
5. Increasing the coordination capacity of the SGG

2025:
The Strategy has a distinct chapter that establishes monitoring and evaluation procedures (The monitoring and evaluation mechanism will be implemented by the Interinstitutional Committee for the development, implementation and monitoring of the National Open Data Strategy and will be developed through specific decisions and the subsequent adoption of working tools. The monitoring and evaluation priorities will relate to: 1. achieving the indicators set out in this Strategy; 2. compliance with the terms assumed by this Strategy; 3. regular reporting, analysis and discussion of reporting results, so that responsible institutions receive rapid and consistent feedback on the good practices they implement, the barriers they need to overcome and the opportunities they need to seize; 4. ensuring transparency of implementation towards all stakeholders; 5. early identification of risks that may jeopardize the proper implementation of this Strategy and the adoption of approaches for their optimal management; 6. identification of working solutions and tools to solve problems arising during implementation; 7. early identification of change needs and adoption of change management processes, including through the revision of the Strategy.) 
These provisions are further complemented by the secondary legislation.

column13:
The Programme of the Prime Minister Marin's Government 2019 aligned that the Government will add depth to the management of information policy (https://valtioneuvosto.fi/en/marin/government-programme/best-public administration-in-the-world). Openness of public information is the overarching principle of information policy. The Government continued resolutely the earlier efforts to open up public information resources, and it drew up a quality criteria (https://www.stat.fi/org/tiedon-laatukehikko/index_en.html) that can facilitate the use of such resources.

Finland has transposed the Directive 2019/1024 on open data and the re-use of public sector information (ODD) by amending the Act on Public Administration Information Management (906/2019) and with the Openness of Government Activities Act (621/1999 with amendments, https://www.finlex.fi/en/laki/kaannokset/1999/en19990621) on the basis of the principle of openness contained in it.

The Openness of Government Activities Act (621/1999 with amendments, https://www.finlex.fi/en/laki/kaannokset/1999/en19990621) provides for the general right to access any official document, including electronic records, in the public domain held by public authorities and private bodies that exercise public authority. Applicants are not required to provide reasons for their request or to verify their identity unless they are requesting personal or other confidential information. Restrictions apply to non-official documents, documents relating to foreign affairs, criminal investigations, police matters, information concerning military intelligence and the armed forces, as well as confidential business activities. According to the Government Programme 2019, the need to update the Openness of Government Activities Act to extend its application to data and information more broadly will be examined. The Ministry of Justice has set up a working group for 2021-2023 for the update of the Openness of Government Activities Act (https://oikeusministerio.fi/julkisuuslain-ajantasaistaminen).

There is a wider information policy report which covers a larger scale of different information policy aspects, including public, private and 3rd sectors. The Report on Ethical Information Policy in an Age of Artificial Intelligence was published on December 2018 (https://vm.fi/en/information-policy-report). It covers open data as a part of information policy and emphasizes equal access to data, while stressing the ethical development of artificial intelligence. The policy goals are fostering the progress of entire society by advancing the creation of new skills and capabilities, encour-aging innovations and innovativeness, and by improving our national competitiveness. Open data is mentioned as one of the strengths of Finland, with wide swathes of public sector data already open, and as one of the policy goals with advance access to data, transferability and compatibility of data across the Single Digital Market. Open data is also inferred as one of the enablers for de-veloping artificial intelligence based on open information and technologies, and as one of the future development potentials, with further open data policies and as part of the future strategy development.
The Act on Public Administration Information Management (906/2019, https://www.finlex.fi/en/laki/kaannokset/2019/en20190906.pdf) aims to ensure harmonised and high-quality management of data as well as secure processing of datasets of authorities to implement the principle of openness. It aims to enable secure and efficient exploitation of the datasets of authorities so that an authority may attend to its tasks and provide its services suc-cessfully and in a qualitative manner in compliance with good governance; and to promote the interoperability of information systems and information resources.

Since 2020 several parliament parties are worked in a free-form and non-political working group with an interest to the cross-party discussion on information policy topics. The Working Group of Information Policy Actors from all parliamentary parties, in short, 'the collaborative group on information policy' tackles topics of interest that come up for discussion both nationally and internationally (https://tietopolitiikka.fi/information-policy-working-group/).

column13:
The nation wide ‘The Opening Up and Using Public Data’ project coordinated by the Ministry of Finance of Finland developed several measures regarding open APIs, technical and semantic interoperability, as well as data quality in order to incentivise and support the publication of and access to real-time or dynamic data. The project created the API Principles to provide common instructions and recommendations for API development by adapting the JRC API Framework into Finnish public administration (https://joinup.ec.europa.eu/collection/api4dt/news/api-framework-implemented-finland/; http://urn.fi/URN:ISBN:978-952-367-915-3). The Act on Information Management in Public Administration (906/2019, https://www.finlex.fi/fi/laki/kaannokset/2019/en20190906.pdf) includes sections of the disclosure of datasets via a technical interface both to the authorities and to other than authorities (Sec. 22 & 24).

The existing Information Policy sets open APIs as a goal for the public sector, because open APIs are seen as the most future-proof way and as an incentive to avoid future maintenance when distributing high-quality always up-to-date and real-time data in a systematic, machine-readable format. New business models and new combinations of skills, from different fields and branches of public and private sector, enabled by the open APIs are seen as additional incentives. Open APIs are also seen as one of the key enablers for future growth.

The mandate to describe and maintain a data inventory is a part of statutory task of maintaining the Information Management Model for the most of the public sector bodies since 2021. According to the Act on Information Management in Public Administration (906/2019, https://www.finlex.fi/fi/laki/kaannokset/2019/en20190906.pdf), each of public sector information management entity shall maintain an information management model, which defines and describes the information management in its operating environment. The Information Management Model is maintained to design and implement the management of services, consideration, and datasets; to implement the rights and restrictions relating to access to information; to decrease multiple collection of information; to implement the interoperability of information systems and information pools; and to maintain information security. The Ministry of Finance of Finland maintains the Public Sector Information Management Map, which describes the data resources to utilise and the procedures for accessing data from the data resources (https://www.exploreadministration.fi/information-management-map-of-public-administration/).

The Act on the Openness of Government Activities (621/1999, https://www.finlex.fi/en/laki/kaannokset/1999/en19990621) mandates the catalogues listing the data inventories to be published as open data. These catalogues give an indication on what each data or information repository holds, for example the City of Vantaa's catalogues of information systems (https://hri.fi/data/fi/dataset/vantaan-kaupungin-tietojarjestelmaluettelo). The dataset provides a list of all information systems in use at the city and information on system ownership, technical responsibility and a brief description of each information system.

The GDPR has also necessitated that all data providers review their data storages and identify personal data for the GDPR coverage, and as part of this review, build the necessary metadata to be able to properly catalogue and identify the data for each data repository.

To make the descriptive metadata of these models and lists better semantically interoperable, data holders and model maintainers, from both public and private sector, can utilise the Interoperability Platform (https://dvv.fi/en/interoperability-platform), a workbench and a set of tools, for defining and describing interoperable data content. The platform consists of glossaries, code sets and data models needed for data flows and in other areas of information management. The tools and the existing data specifications are available free of charge for terminology work, management of code sets, and data modelling. Data content producers are responsible for their own data specifications and their quality, and for keeping them up to date.

column13:
The governance model is three-pronged, formed by the Information Management Board of Public Administration, the Ministry of Finance, and the sector-specific Ministries.

The Board is appointed by the government for a term of four years at a time, and is composed of members who have expertise in information management, the transparency requirements of public documents, IT systems, data pools, interoperability and statistical methods. The Ministry of Finance provides the secretariat of the Board. The Board's task is to promote best practices in applying the Act on Information Management in Public Administration and report on its application to the government biannually. The Board is also tasked with evaluating the application of the Open Data Directive's requirements nationally.

The Ministry of Finance is responsible for directing the interoperability of public administration datasets and information systems, and maintaining the Information Management Map of public administration, as well as creating general guidelines.

Sector-specific Ministries are responsible for keeping the Information Management Map up to date for their sector and providing sector-specific guidelines on interoperability.

column6:
How would you classify the model used for governing open data in your country? 

For Explanation:
*  Please briefly explain why this model was chosen/works best for your country
column13:
2024:
Open data governance in the public administration is arranged as a part of common information management governance. The Act on Information Management in Public Administration (906/2019, https://www.finlex.fi/fi/laki/kaannokset/2019/en20190906.pdf) creates a common governance model and instruments to steer, encourage and support public administration's information management including open data. A specific open data governance model is not included in the act. Thus, open data is considered to be an integrated part of any organisation’s or information management entity’s work flow or data resources. 

Governance of publishing data is out of the act’s scope and publishing processes are regulated, among other statutes, by the Openness of Government Activities Act (621/1999 with amendments, https://www.finlex.fi/en/laki/kaannokset/1999/en19990621). It provides for the general right to access any official document, including electronic records, in the public domain held by public authorities and private bodies that exercise public authority. Restrictions apply to non-official documents, documents relating to foreign affairs, criminal investigations, police matters, information concerning military intelligence and the armed forces, as well as confidential business activities.

As a result of the constitutional order in Finland, an all-encompassing top down structure is not viable. The roles and tasks of governance takes place naturally on the various levels of public administration and public sector activities, as municipalities, welfare counties and central government authorities have independence and autonomy in applying and interpreting law. 

The national open data portal, Opendata.fi, focuses on guidance and assistance of data providers rather than trying to carry out or organise the various efforts to open data.

The fiscal situation in the Finnish public sector has reduced the available resources for new projects or initiatives.

An employee has the right, based on a statute, to take study leave in one or more periods, full time or part time, for at most two years during a period of five years, if his or her full-time employment relationship with the same employer has lasted for at least one year in one or more periods. If the employment relationship has lasted for less than a year but at least three months, the employee is entitled to take study leave for a maximum of five days.

Several universities, open universities and colleges has included lectures and courses about open data and its applications in their curriculas to support and to create possibilities to learn and to gain information about open data (https://www.avoin.jyu.fi/opinto-opas/fi/opintojakso/itkp9102/; https://fitech.io/fi/opinnot/data-ja-vuorovaikutus/; https://research.tuni.fi/researchdata/trainings/ ; https://research.tuni.fi/datapalvelu/menneet-koulutukset-2022/; ). There is also e-learning modules with open data related content in the public administration's e-learning portal (eOppiva.fi). Part of the courses are available as science for all, open university or MOOC courses. For SME's there was the Growth from Data (Datasta kasvua) serie of webinars (https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLFMs9Qmp5uLJHszrDcuCAricrk0tcQ33s). A specific curricula for open data studies does not exist.

Government agencies has purchased specific open data training and courses how to prepare for and to open data assets from different companies and associations. The Statistics Finland has also provided trainings. The 'Opening Up and Using Public Sector Data' project created an user-driven action model for public administration to identify, prioritize and open up information together with stakeholders (https://www.avoindata.fi/en/operating-model). The model will be enriched with available, useful material, for example from the European Data Portal. The project also created e-learning courses on the model but also on data interoperability and data quality. These courses are freely available on the public administration e-learning portal eOppiva (https://www.eoppiva.fi/kokoelmat/dealing-with-data-more-efficient-use-of-information/). Anyone interested can launch these e-learning materials at their convenience.

The cities of Helsinki Region Area (hri.fi) arrange training events about 8-10 times a year to the public servants of the cities in the capital region. For training materials, see https://hri.fi/fi/ohjeet/datan-avaajalle/koulutusmateriaalia/.

There are also plans to begin cooperation to produce open data training materials within the Digital and Population Data Services Agency, deployed by two of its services and teams, the National Open Data Portal, opendata.fi, and the Finnish Service Catalog, (https://www.suomi.fi/services/suomi-fi-finnish-service-catalogue-digital-and-population-data-services-agency/d93be162-07a2-45f2-84b3-f794da852b58), to get further assistance on creating materials.

Due to the EU Data Protection Regulation, we can no longer use for example https://disqus.com/, as it is headquartered in the US and does not comply with the EU Data Protection Regulation. For Explanation:
* If yes, what are the main causes for the lack of DCAT-AP compliance?
column13:
The reasons for incompatibility have been the same fora number of years: 
1 = Very old data sets that are published before DCAT-AP 1.1 are not necessarily compliant if they have not received any content or metadata updates. 
2 =  Some data owners provide minimum metadata descriptions only (although we recommend a comprehensive set of metadata). We do not mandate filling in the recommended or optional fields when submitting new data sets. 
3 =  For some harvested data sets (esp. geospatial data), the metadata available does not match the DCAT-AP metadata 100%, and we support only partial GeoDCAT-AP compliance for the time being.
4 = A large number of data sets (esp. geospatial data) carries additional metadata derived e.g. from Inspire and its national applications that is not explicitly identified in the DCAT-AP specification. The majority of this data can be mapped in the recommended fields, which we have done e.g. with Paikkatietohakemisto. 
- Any new materials either harvested or added in the portal directly are, however, compliant at least with the DCAT-AP 2 mandatory properties.

Do you use a model (such as the 5-Star Open Data or FAIR) to assess the quality of deployment of data in your country?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe.
column13:
Opendata.fi assesses the quality of the data according to the 5-star model. Based on discussions with the data openers at the time of answering, both data publishers and open data re-users consider the model cumbersome and difficult and  thus a barrier for publication. A lot of typical open data re-users (e.g. regular citizens and reporters in media) use open data in very basic/proprietary formats, such as MS Excel. 

We are increasingly trying to apply the FAIR principles in assessing the data quality and related communications to the extent that is possible. Implementing the principles in the national portal is not clear cut, but we aim for higher adoption. 

Opendata.fi also considers it problematic that the data semantics in the 5-star model are not anchored with anything. The semantics do not, for example foster interoperability of data on national (Finnish) or European levels. The portal team’s experience has, however, shown that the best publishing approach is either three stars or five stars on the 5-Star model.

The Finnish Meteorological Institute provides most of its datasets open, free of change, in WMS format and some in Amazon AWS S3 format through the FMI Open Data Services since 2013. More information on the FMI website: https://en.ilmatieteenlaitos.fi/open-data. 

An impact study focusing on data usage in 2018 and a user survey on the FMI Open Data Services was conducted in 2019 which proved the value of open data information for business, public sector, and citizens. According to the study, FMI open data has a significant impact on business. 14% of the private company respondents said that FMI open data have generated new business during last 3 years (N = 389; 14 % of 389 = 54 companies). 

User survey and impact study results

Use of open meteorological data through the FMI Open Data Services:
- Most users use interpolated timeseries
- Large datasets are disseminated via AWS and it’s important for heavy users
- Timeseries API is crucial
- Summer is the busiest time of the year (three times more data requests)
- Removing of API-key increased significantly data requests
- Guidelines and manuals were used by approx. 60% of the users
- 25% of respondents use FMI open data with other open data  
- Four top datasets cover over 3/4 of requests:
o Station specific weather observations
o Weather forecast model HIRLAM (production was terminated in late 2022)
o Lightning strikes
o Weather radar images

Users of the FMI Open Data Services:
- Over 60% of users couldn’t be recognized. However, 80% of recognized users were companies and only 6% from public sector. 
- The companies requested mostly weather forecasts and surface observations and public sector used a lot of road weather observations

FMI Open Data Services is used for example in:
- teaching students in the elementary and high school
- water supply and waste management services, especially for forecasting waste-water flow 
- displaying real-time and historical marine weather data as background information in our services for the users
- estimating solar power production

Access to FMI Open Data Services

Access to FMI open datasets through the web interfaces:
• Discovery Service (a.k.a. Catalog service) providing metadata about the available data sets and services, implemented using the OGC Catalog Service for Web (CSW),
• View Services giving a visual preview of the available data sets, implemented using OGC Web Map Service (WMS), and
• Download Services providing a continuous online access to the most up-to-date data, implemented using OGC Web Feature Service (WFS).

More technical guidance about the FMI Open Data Services: https://en.ilmatieteenlaitos.fi/open-data-manual.

2024:
The national open data policy, reflected in Law 37 on the re-use of public sector information, has been aligned with new European guidelines. The last update took place on 9 May 2023. See here: https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2007-19814&tn=1&p=20230509. 
This amendment is reflected in the fifth additional provision of Regulation (EU) 2022/868 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 30 May 2022 on European data governance and amending Regulation (EU) 2018/1724 (Data Governance Regulation). See here: https ://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2007-19814&tn=1&p=20230509#:~:text=%5BBloque%2025%3A%20%23dtunica%5D
Likewise, on 27 February 2024, as reflected in Royal Decree 210/2024, the Directorate General for Data and the Directorate General for Digitalisation and Artificial Intelligence, management bodies under the Secretary of State for Digitalisation and Artificial Intelligence of the recently created Ministry for Digital Transformation and the Civil Service, were set up.
1. The Directorate General for Data, as referred to in article 4, is constituted as the unit in charge of promoting the use of data by Public Administrations, companies and citizens, as well as the sharing of data in interoperable data spaces, contributing to the development of the digital single market for Europe, in coordination with the competent sectorial ministerial departments and in collaboration with the Autonomous Communities and Local Entities. 
2. The Directorate General for Digitalisation and Artificial Intelligence, as stated in article 3, assumes among its functions the definition and coordinated management of programmes and actions, boosting and promoting I+D+i in the field of artificial intelligence, including the coordination of the application of open data to artificial intelligence and other digital enabling technologies in the productive sectors of the economy and society.
2023:
Spain has had a national open data policy since 2007. This open data policy has been evolving in accordance with the guidelines set by Europe. This policy is reflected in Law 37/2007

In addition to the aforementioned regulatory framework, Spain has a series of strategic documents that reinforce the open data policy for the 2020-2025 period. These documents include:

- The Digital Agenda for 2025, which contemplates the implementation of a National Artificial Intelligence Strategy that includes measures related to the availability of open data, which are essential for the correct operation and training of Artificial Intelligence systems.
- The Digitalization Plan for Public Administrations 2021-2025, which highlights the intention to evolve the model of access to public and private information to facilitate the development of high value-added services, based on the work developed by the Aporta Initiative.
- The IV Open Government Plan of Spain 2020-2024, which includes actions such as the improvement of real-time access to dynamic data through appropriate technical means and the promotion of data sets with high reuse value through their selection, the definition of common vocabularies and their publication.
Likewise, the Data Office, which assumes the governance policies and standards in data management and analysis that should govern the General State Administration, is working on a national data strategy and an update of the national open data strategy. See more: https://www.boe.es/eli/es/o/2020/07/31/etd803

The following three innovative actions carried out in recent months (2024-2025) linked to the National Open Data Strategy should be highlighted:
1. Development of the Implementation Guide of the DCAT-AP-ES profile, DCAT application profile for Spain that takes as reference DCAT-AP 2.1.1 together with the elements described in the extension DCAT-AP HVD 2.2.0, in order to incorporate the modelling of the High Value Datasets. See here: https://datosgobes.github.io/DCAT-AP-ES/
2.- Redesign and enrichment of the datos.gob.es platform, the national open data platform. It is currently in the production start-up phase. It will be released later this year. See here: https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/dimension1_2025_evidencia_p2_1.png. 
Among other functionalities and developments, we highlight the following five:

•	Views of contents/datasets by sector of activity. See example for the "Culture and Leisure" sector here: See here: https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/dimension1_2025_evidencia_p2_3.png
•	Significant improvements in the usability of key sections such as the Data Request Channel. https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/dimension1_2025_evidencia_p2_4.png
•	Increased visibility of high-value data (HVD). See here: https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/dimension1_2025_evidencia_p2_5.png

3.- Implementation of a personalised service of technical and economic support to the General State Administration for the provision of public data:  the Public Data Demand Management Project. 2024:
2024:
By the end of 2023, the national action plan (national strategy) for open data, whose actions are reflected in the datos.gob.es platform, has been complemented by:
- The creation of the Single National Information Point. This channel responds to the obligation set by the Data Governance Regulation for member countries. 
This channel is a mechanism to encourage the re-use of public sector data that, for certain reasons, cannot be made available as open data because it is protected for reasons of statistical or commercial confidentiality, intellectual property rights, or privacy issues. See here: https://datos.gob.es/es/acceso-nsip
- The recently approved Artificial Intelligence Strategy includes an important initiative linked to the Common Data Governance of the General State Administration. The objective pursued is the development of specialised language models that enable the development of applications for deployment in the public sector. The initiative determines that a common governance model will be established for the data and documentary corpus of the NSA to guarantee the standards of security, quality, interoperability and reuse of all data. See point 5.3 Common data governance of the NSA: https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/consejodeministros/resumenes/Documents/2024/140524-Estrategia%20de%20Inteligencia%20Artificial%202024-completa.pdf.
- Royal Decree-Law 6/2023, of 19 December, which approves urgent measures for the implementation of the Recovery, Transformation and Resilience Plan for the public service of justice, civil service, local government and patronage, stresses the general principle of data orientation, referring to how: data are key to modern public policies. Data management will enable or facilitate the interoperability of systems, electronic processing, data search and analysis, anonymisation and pseudonymisation, dashboarding, document management and transformation, publication of information on open data portals, production of automated, assisted and proactive actions, use of artificial intelligence systems for public policy making, and transmission of data as determined.
2023:
Spain has a national open data action plan (national strategy) that is developed in accordance with the following principles:

- Vision: Promote the opening of public information in Spain through innovative and structuring actions in a global environment of collaboration with public and private partners.
- Mission: Make Spain a national and international benchmark for the opening of public information and the promoting of open data as a key element for improving the standard of living of citizens, the competitiveness of companies and the efficiency of public administrations.
- Objectives: 
o Generate relationships between the actors of the national and international open data ecosystem.
o Create awareness of the value of public data and its re-use, covering sectors in which innovation with data is presented as a key element.
o Guide publishers and re-users on the actions to be carried out in order to contribute to the success of the actions based on data they use.
o Identify business models, re-use companies and start-up success stories in order to favour the extrapolation of successful practices.
o Improve recognition of the public sector efforts on a national scale by making the data generated from this activity available to society.

.- The actions to develop fall within the following lines of action:
1.	Awareness and dissemination of the culture of data management, analysis and exploitation
2.	Sectoral Analysis and Statistics
3.	Regulation on the re-use of public sector information
4.	Strengthening of national cooperation
5.	Strengthening of international cooperation
6.	Enrichment and maintenance of the National Catalogue of reusable public information and support services
7.	Support for Innovation in the creation of data-based products and services

More info: https://datos.gob.es/es/acerca-de-la-iniciativa-aporta

2025:
Open data policies at regional and local level are usually embedded in broader governance, public innovation or digital government strategies. 
Therefore, as a complement to the examples of open data policies and strategies already mentioned in the responses to previous editions of the questionnaire, it is worth mentioning the most recent Open Government Strategies, which encompass strategic plans linked to open data. Three of these are listed below: 
•	Fourth open government plan of the Madrid City Council (2024-2027). See here: https://transparencia.madrid.es/FWProjects/transparencia/PlanesYMemorias/Planes/PlanGobiernoAbierto/IVPlan/ficheros/IVPlanGobiernoAbiertoAyuntamientoMadrid.pdf
The paper highlights the importance of open data as a key pillar for transparency and innovation. Madrid City Council is committed to improving the quality and accessibility of the data published on its Open Data Portal, encouraging its reuse. The aim is to create a more visual and understandable platform, with relevant information for citizens. In addition, collaboration with professional re-users and the academic community will be promoted to maximise the value of open data.
•	I Action Plan of the Government of Navarre for the Open Government Partnership (OGP). See here: https://gobiernoabierto.navarra.es/sites/default/files/assets/files/planes-programas/I%20Plan%20Acci%C3%B3n%20del%20Gobieno%20de%20Navarra%20para%20la%20OGP.pdf
The document underlines the importance of open data for transparency and citizen participation. Navarra has implemented free software programmes such as CKAN, Drupal and Decidim to facilitate access to public data. In addition, it has published data from various entities and has collaborated in the reform of the State Transparency Law. The aim is to improve the quality of the data and to encourage its re-use by citizens and other stakeholders.
•	Open Data Strategy 2021-2024 of the Government of the Balearic Islands. See here: https://www.caib.es/sites/opendatacaib/es/estrategia_datos_abiertos_goib/
The Government of the Balearic Islands promotes the reuse of public information to foster transparency and citizen participation. The 2021-2024 open data strategy includes the opening of data in interoperable formats, the designation of responsible persons in each department, and the promotion of data quality and use. Priority is given to the publication of data in strategic sectors such as health and education, and interoperability with other data portals is encouraged.
2024:
2024:
The trend in Spain is evolving to consider the open data strategy as part of a data governance strategy. This approach ensures the success and sustainability of open data strategies over time. 
Therefore, as a complement to the examples of open data policies and strategies already mentioned, it is worth mentioning the data governance strategies being implemented by numerous administrations in Spain, which include specific actions linked to open plans. 
The following are examples of such strategies involving open data:
- The Basque Government has published the BAC public sector data governance strategy. See here: https://www.euskadi.eus/contenidos/informacion/estrateg_gobernanza_del_dato2/es_def/adjuntos/estrategia_de_gobernanza_de_los_datos_es.pdf

· Decree 84/2023 regulating the data governance and management model for administrative purposes. See here: https://www3.gobiernodecanarias.org/juriscan/ficha.jsp?id=79252
· Decree 88/2023 establishing the reference model for strategic planning and management and management by objectives. See here: https://www3.gobiernodecanarias.org/juriscan/ficha.jsp?id=79253
Also, over the last months, several bodies have published Public Sector Information Re-use Plans and Ordinances, linked to their open data policies. These include the following: 
- Ponferrada City Council: https://opendata.ponferrada.org/. Action carried out in accordance with the Plan of measures to promote the reuse of information in Ponferrada City Council: https://opendata.ponferrada.org/iniciativa-ponferrada-30/plan-de-reutilizacion
- Mutualidad General de Funcionarios Civiles del Estado: develops its open data portal: https://www.muface.es/muface_Home/muface/DATOS-ABIERTOS.html  according to a recently published re-use plan: https://www.muface.es/muface_Home/dam/jcr:91d0f33e-c421-487a-a108-21897ffcbeff/PLANDATOSABIERTOSYREUTILIZACIONVERSWEB.pdf
- Pinto City Council: develops its open data portal: https://gobiernoabierto.ayto-pinto.es/datos-abiertos-de-pinto according to a recently published reuse plan: https://gobiernoabierto.ayto-pinto.es/documents/1067857/1773798/Estrategia+y+Plan+Accion+Datos+Abiertos+AytoPinto+2022+reducido.pdf/8888d790-4248-436c-87d9-73321dd19272
- Government of the Balearic Islands: Agreement of the Governing Council of 17 April 2023 establishing measures to promote openness and re-use of data: https://www.caib.es/sites/opendatacaib/f/421020
2023:
Taking into account the guidelines set by national policy in Spain, regional and local administrations have been developing specific open data policies and strategies that complement the work developed at the national level. The following are examples of recent cases corresponding to each of the three levels of administration:

o At the local level, the data strategy of the City Council of Valencia seeks a paradigm shift in the city in terms of the provision and management of open data and encourages the opening of quality public and private data and information. More info: https://www.administracionpublicadigital.es/proyectos/2022/07/valencia-presenta-su-nueva-estrategia-de-datos-abiertos

o At the regional level, in June 2022 the Generalitat Valenciana took decisive steps on the path of open government, which are based on an ambitious open data strategy to produce complete and effective transparency, to enable results-based management and accountability, and to generate a network of relationships with different segments of reusers that can give value to the data and contribute to social, economic, environmental and democratic development.  Más info: https://portaldadesobertes.gva.es/documents/170052220/175652610/2022.06.01+Estrategia+post+consulta+revisada+DG.pdf/a54c9fcc-3559-41fa-9665-f7086af3501f

o At the central administration level, in November 2022, the Ministry of Justice launches the initiative called Data-driven Justice whose main purpose is the creation of a secure, interoperable and reuse-oriented public data space. Among other objectives, it establishes that, given that data must be considered a public good, it is considered a priority to guarantee free access to them. More info: https://datos.gob.es/en/blog/data-and-digital-transformation-justice-system
In addition to these examples, other strategies can be found in the column "Open data strategy" of the following file: https://datos.gob.es/es/iniciativas/csv

Work is currently underway to complement the National Open Data Policy Action Plan with the signing of an agreement between the Secretary of State for Digitalisation and Artificial Intelligence and the public business entity Red.es to promote the reuse of public sector information and the data economy.
The Agreement is aimed at fostering the openness, re-use and governance of public sector information, with special attention to the State Public Sector, in coordination with the rest of the autonomous and local administrations in Spain, promoting the data economy and, in particular, the creation of new products and services, in collaboration with the private sector and civil society, for the benefit of society.  
The four-year agreement will be published in the Official State Gazette in the coming months. See here: https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/dimension1_2025_evidencia_p4.png
2024:
2024:
The 2024-2025 action plan of the national open data policy includes, for each policy area, the following relevant developments:
o AWARENESS RAISING ACTIONS
- Disseminate data and open data through the social network Instagram. The aim is to reach younger audiences between 16 and 35 years of age and thus raise awareness among the younger generation of the value of the great asset that is open data.  See here: https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/dimension1_2024_evidencia_p4.png
- Develop podcast interviews with experts in the field of data and open data. They will last between 15 and 20 minutes. Each interview will be associated with a 3–4-minute promotional video interview for use on social media.
o ANALYSIS AND STATISTICS ACTIONS
- Expansion and enrichment through Power BI report of the activity report offered to the public on the activity taking place in the National Open Data Catalogue and on the datos.gob.es platform. 
o REGULATORY ACTIONS
- Within the framework of actions linked to the Technical Interoperability Standard for the reuse of information resources, publication in the Official State Gazette of the DCAT-AP-ES and the associated application guide.
o NATIONAL and INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION ACTIONS
- Significant improvements in the map of initiatives published on datos.gob.es in terms of functionality and content. To enrich the representation, the mapping functionalities of Power BI will be used. To expand on the information provided, the answers provided by the administrations to the following questionnaire, Assessment of the reusable public data ecosystem in Spain 2024, will be used. See here: https://datos.gob.es/es/evaluacion-del-ecosistema-de-los-datos-publicos-reutilizables-en-espana-2024
o ACTIONS LINKED TO NATIONAL CATALOGUE AND SUPPORT
- We are working on a new version of the platform linked to the open data policy of the    Spanish government, with the aim of evolving the components of the current platform, im-proving its functionality, usability and accessibility, and responding to the obligations set by the current European regulations on open data, bringing together initiatives around the data with special attention to data spaces. It will take into account the obligations set in the scope of Directive (EU) 2019/1024 of the European Parliament and of the Council and the DCAT application profile for metadata catalogues in its latest consolidated version. To this end, the ‘Advanced Service for the new Datos.gob.es platform’ 024/23-SI has been tendered for 4 years for the value of 2,305,761.39 euros. See here: https://contrataciondelestado.es/wps/portal/!ut/p/b0/04_Sj9CPykssy0xPLMnMnMz0vMAfIjU1JTC3Iy87KtUlJLEnNyUuNzMpMzSxKTgQr0w_Wj9KMyU1zLcvQjk0qKSr3K3bxSc1ydAoKcKqJM8rxUDdJtbfULcnMdATu3a7M!/

o	INNOVATION ACTIONS
- The novel innovation action for the period 2024-2025 is associated with the development of complex, step-by-step documented open data analyses. The activity is presented as a training action that demonstrates the value of this asset when it comes to generating knowledge that helps innovation. To date, data visualisations have been carried out. For the new period, data analysis of a certain technical complexity is sought. See example here: https://datos.gob.es/es/documentacion/ruta-la-electrificacion-descifrando-el-crecimiento-del-vehiculo-electrico-en-espana
2023:

The open data strategy update, which is in the process of final approval, includes a set of actions. 

See here: https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/dimension1_2023_evidenciapregunta_3.png

From the key actions, in the action plan for the 2022-2023 period, the focus will be on the following:

o AWARENESS RAISING ACTIONS
.-> New 2023-24:
a.1. Development of materials linked to the latest European guidelines on high-value data, data Governance Act, data spaces, ethical use of data, etc. 
.-> In progress:
a.2. Development of materials of different nature aimed at:
-- Sensitize society as a whole about the value of data.
-- Enhance data production, sharing and use. 
-- Amplify the efforts made by administrations, companies and individuals in the promotion of data culture.
-- Generate synergies between publishers and reusers of data
-- Establish datos.gob.es as a reference in the field of data and open data.
-- Contribute to consolidate the data communities, and especially the community Contribute as a framework and reference for open public information initiatives in Spain.

a.3. Analysis of the communication strategy and actions carried out by other national and international initiatives, with the aim of strengthening collaboration ties and learning from the good practices of others.

o ANALYSIS AND STATISTICAL ACTIONS
.-> New 2023-24
b.1. X-ray of unmet open data needs. Remediation actions
.-> In progress:
b.2. Analysis of the evolution over time of the growth and queries by sector and by level of administration to the datasets housed in the National Catalog.
b.3. Prospective studies to guide agencies to publish data in line with what is being published by counterpart agencies in other countries.

o REGULATORY ACTIONS
.-> New 2023-24
c.1. Publication of the list of High Value Data Sets (HVDS) by the Data Office beyond those established at European level.
.-> In progress:
c.2. Evolution of the Adjustments of the Technical Standard for interoperability of information reuse in force in Spain towards the DCAT v2.0.1 application profile, and integration with consensus vocabularies on 40 datasets that are established as a reference in the context of smat cities. 

o NATIONAL and INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION ACTIONS
.-> New 2023-24
d.1. Empowerment of the NSDI as a central access point to all national geodata, consolidating information from different sources. Integration with sectoral and open source information from spatial observation.
.-> In progress:
d.2. Intensification of international cooperation, especially with the new European data portal.
d.3. Search for synergies with the digitization and data strategies that are being implemented both globally and by many public organizations.
d.5. Collaboration, participation/joint organization in events, and reinforcement of actions with business associations (e.g. ASEDIE) and civil society organizations.

o ACTIONS LINKED TO THE NATIONAL CATALOGUE AND SUPPORT
.-> New 2023-24
d.1. Evolution of the current platform to a new space in which open data coexist with shared data initiatives launched by different organizations.
.-> In progress:
e.2. Improve the visibility of high-value data offered through APIs, real-time data, as well as the quality of metadata accompanying published data.
e.3. Enrich the interactive map of open data initiatives in Spain: increase in the number of initiatives and information related to each of the initiatives referenced.
e.4. Evolution of the Adjustments to the Technical Standard for interoperability of information reuse in force in Spain in terms of typification of the conditions of use, incorporation of metadata agreed upon geo DCAT, stat DCAT, and integration with vocabularies agreed upon on 40 datasets that are established as a reference in the context of smat cities. 

o INNOVATION ACTIONS 
.-> New 2023-24
f.1. Development on the new platform of the Business Radar, a space from which to give visibility to national initiatives that promote data sharing and/or foster ecosystems that enable the creation of new data-driven products and services.
.-> In progress:
f.1. Promote engagement with communities of developers of open data-based solutions to analyze trends and identify needs and develop data science exercises and publish on the project's Github account (https://github.com/datosgobes).

•	At local government level, this refers to the local councils that report that they are in the process of preparing (or updating) the annual questionnaire assessing the activity carried out by public administrations in Spain in the area of open data. Specifically, the following municipalities have confirmed that they are working on it: Teba Town Council, Tenerife Island Council, Manlleu Town Council, Viladecans Town Council and L'Hospitalet de Llobregat Town Council.
2024:
2024:
Recently, the Generalitat de Catalunya, through the Directorate General for Open Data, Transparency and Collaboration, has drawn up a single inventory of databases as an ordered and descriptive register of each one of the data files available in the Administration of the Generalitat de Catalunya and in the entities of its public sector. See here: https://administraciodigital.gencat.cat/ca/dades/dades-obertes/projectes/inventari-de-dades/

Likewise, the Spanish Federation of Municipalities and Provinces (FEMP) approved at the end of 2023 a standard ordinance for local entities to establish their strategy on transparency and data governance. Article 9 of the standard ordinance establishes the requirement for local authorities to create an Inventory of datasets and information sources. Specifically, it establishes that "the Administration of the local authority shall have an Inventory of data sets and sources of information, the content, format and means for management of which shall be adapted to the size and complexity of the local authority [...]" As descriptive information on data sets and sources of information, the following should be included as far as possible: 
(a) Name and description of the data set. 
(b) the body or unit responsible for its management. 
(c) where appropriate, its constituent subsets and relationships or dependencies with other data sets. 
d) Fields, indicating which are mandatory and which are optional. 
(e) where appropriate, spatial resolution and level of disaggregation, with the applicable mini-mum threshold, where applicable. 
(f) information that facilitates the understanding of the data. 
(g) Minimum and, where appropriate, recommended update frequency. 
(h) the format(s) in which it is available, as well as any data structures, vocabularies or taxon-omies used, where appropriate.
i) In the data obtained, the origin or origins, including, where appropriate, the URL or URI, and the method of collection, with an indication of the reliability and other relevant circumstances. In the data generated, the methods and algorithms used. 
(j) if it contains personal data, a link to the information on it contained in the register of pro-cessing activities. 
(k) where appropriate, the categories of administrative acts and other decisions which are gen-erated automatically from the data, with the information provided for in Article 23(3). 
l) If applicable, the periodicity and form of generation of the historical files. 
m) A standard unique identifier, preferably the DOI. 
(n) the repository where it is kept and the computerised means used for its management. 

See more here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1vam_TAcMrdXr0oKwbiFq1OyHpngi1Lpb/view
2023:
The Spanish Government's open data strategy, currently under revision, requires administrations to publish data on the General State Administration's data platform, which functions as a data inventory. This publication must be made under service conditions that enable both access to the data within the Administration and access to the general public.  

The objective is to advance in the role of administrations as consumers of information generated from other agencies, as reflected in the internal document: Inventory of Information Reuse Data of February 2023. See here: https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/dimension1_2023_evidenciapregunta_9a.png

This data inventory is based on the following conviction: "The action and communication of administrations can be more effective, more transparent and more sustainable if they are based on valid and solid data provided in real time at the time of decision making.  An intensive use of data allows to boost innovation in public sector actions, facilitating the contrast of ideas, promoting creativity and the maximum use of resources in the general framework of a modern, participative, open and useful public management to solve or improve social problems and challenges".

Is there a governance structure in place that enables the participation and/or inclusion of various open data stakeholders? 

For Explanation:
*  If yes, please briefly describe the governance structure and its operating model
column13:
2025:
Data governance in Spain is mainly led by the Directorate General for Data, which reports to the Secretary of State for Digitalisation and Artificial Intelligence of the Ministry for Digital Transformation and Public Administration. The mission of the Directorate General for Data is to promote the use of data by Public Administrations, companies and citizens, as well as the sharing of data in interoperable data spaces, contributing to the development of the single digital market for Europe, in coordination with the competent sectorial ministerial depart-ments and in collaboration with the Autonomous Communities and Local Entities.

As a result of this role of dialogue and coordination, the Interministerial Working Group on Data was set up three years ago, which is presented as a Knowledge Community that meets monthly to discuss data and open data. Various open data stakeholders, including business-es, are invited to this working group. See here: https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/dimension1_2025_evidencia_p13.png

In addition, a data working group has been established within the Interministerial Commission for Connectivity and Digitalization with formal representatives from all ministries. It defines actions aimed at promoting data in the public and private sectors. 

Likewise, the Directorate General for Public Governance has been working in recent months on the configuration of the V Open Government Plan, which will be published in the coming months. This plan will give birth to new initiatives linked to open data resulting from a co-creation process developed on the basis of an already consolidated governance structure, and involving all open data stakeholders. See here information about the process: https://transparencia.gob.es/transparencia/transparencia_Home/index/Gobierno-abierto/planes-accion/VPLAN.html

In addition to all this, the national open data strategy, which is reflected in the datos.gob.es platform, manages the relationship with the different stakeholders in open data matters on a daily basis: companies, civic organisations and citizens in general, in accordance with the governance scheme that can be seen here: https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/iniciativaaporta_modelogobernanza_2021_2022.pdf
2024:
Data governance in Spain is mainly led by the Directorate General for Data, which re-ports to the Secretary of State for Digitalisation and Artificial Intelligence of the Minis-try for Digital Transformation and the Civil Service. The mission of the Directorate General for Data is to promote the use of data by Public Administrations, companies and citizens, as well as the sharing of data in interoperable data spaces, contributing to the development of the single digital market for Europe, in coordination with the competent sectorial ministerial departments and in collaboration with the Autono-mous Communities and Local Entities. Among others, the following functions will be carried out:

a) Dialogue and coordination with the agents representing the data economy and participation in commissions, working groups and other international or national data forums, both public and private, and including national representation in the European Data Innovation Committee.
b) Coordination and monitoring of the strategies, plans, programmes and any other initiative around digitalisation of the different ministerial departments and dependent entities, promoting data-oriented design, their effectiveness, efficiency and impact, as well as their alignment with the framework of the strategies and programmes of the European Union and other international organisations.
c) The design, implementation and monitoring of strategies, plans, programmes and any other initiative for the promotion of mass use and sharing of data between companies, citizens and the public sector, as well as for the promotion of the development and deployment of data spaces in the productive sectors of the economy.
d) The design, development, promotion and monitoring of policies and governance schemes, reference models, federated catalogues of data sets and resources, technical standards and technologies that foster the data economy in the productive sectors of the economy.
e) The promotion and dissemination of best practices and valuable data initiatives, as well as the development of knowledge transfer mechanisms, in particular within ministerial departments and public administrations.
f) Openness and re-use in public administrations, coordinating the management of the access point and the making available of high value public datasets.
g) The design, promotion, coordination and monitoring of strategies, plans, programmes and initiatives that foster research, development and innovation in technologies, services and products for the data economy, contributing to the development of a competitive national industry, in collaboration with the rest of the relevant entities.
Some of these competences are reinforced in Initiative 5.3 Common NSA data governance of the recently published Artificial Intelligence Strategy, which states that: “It is necessary to address regulation from a comprehensive legislative approach, developing a data governance model. Indeed, this regulatory drive for effective data governance in the NSA will include the overall design of a data-oriented organisational structure, with the new Directorate General for Data of the Secretary of State for Digitalisation and Artificial Intelligence as the backbone and enabler.". See here:
https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/consejodeministros/resumenes/Documents/2024/140524-Estrategia%20de%20Inteligencia%20Artificial%202024-completa.pdf

The Directorate General for Data is also closely involved in the national open data strategy, the Aporta Initiative, whose team manages the relationship with the other open data stakeholders: companies, civic organisations and citizens in general, according to the governance scheme which can be found here: https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/iniciativaaporta_modelogobernanza_2021_2022.pdf

Bottom-up coordination is developed through periodic meetings and active listening actions through which the requests of local entities and organizations closely linked to citizens, such as the Network of local entities for transparency and citizen participation of the Spanish Federation of Municipalities and Provinces, and the Association of infomediary companies (ASEDIE) (bottom-up), are attended to.

f) Openness and re-use in public administrations, coordinating the management of the access point and the making available of high value public datasets.

See here: https://www.gandia.es/aytg/web_php/txt/OrdenancaCAS.pdf
2024:
2024:
Over the last 12 months, some public administrations have started to set up the unit responsible for information referred to in "Article 10.bis. Unit responsible for information" of the consolidated text of Law 37/2007, of 16 November, on the re-use of public sector information, which transposes Directive (EU) 2019/1160 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 20 June 2019 into Spanish law. Specifically:
The Government of the Canary Islands refers that "Work is currently underway to select the most appropriate instrument for the application of Article 10.bis on the Unit responsible for information, which will coordinate the re-use of public sector information (RISP) in the Government of the Canary Islands and its public institutional sector". See here: https://transparencia.gob.es/transparencia/transparencia_Home/index/Gobierno-abierto/seguimientoIVPlanGA/seguimiento_C10/Canarias/10-28-2-DatosAbiertos.html
The Government of the Balearic Islands, in its Government Council Agreement of 17 April 2023 establishing measures to promote openness and re-use of data, refers to its intention to: "(d) Collaborate with freedom of information / access to information / right to information units to align the proactive release of open data with governments' obligation to release information on request." See here: https://www.caib.es/sites/opendatacaib/f/421020
The Denia Town Council, in its Ordinance on transparency, access to information and reuse of information, provides for its creation and recalls that "citizens have the rights set out in Article 4, which may be exercised in person or by telematic means under equal conditions, with the creation of a unit responsible for public information being foreseen in all cases". See here: https://www.denia.es/adjuntos/normativa/ord_transparencia_c.pdf
The Gandía Town Council in its Municipal Ordinance on transparency, access to information and reuse of data, refers to the following: The City Council shall designate a Public Information Unit (PIU), with competence over transparency, re-use and access to information. See here: https://www.gandia.es/aytg/web_php/txt/OrdenancaCAS.pdf
2023:
In accordance with "Article 10.bis. Unit responsible for information" of the consolidated text of Law 37/2007, of November 16, on the reuse of public sector information, which incorporates into Spanish law Directive (EU) 2019/1160 of the European Parliament and of the Council of June 20, 2019, it is mandatory for all public administrations to determine a Unit responsible for ensuring the availability of their information. Ver en: https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2007-19814#:~:text=%5B-,Bloque%2017%3A%20%23a1%2D2%5D,-Art%C3%ADculo%2010.bis
The Unit responsible for information in each agency has the following functions:
a) Coordinate information reuse activities with existing policies on publications, administrative information and electronic administration.
b) Provide information on the competent bodies, within its scope, for the reception, processing and resolution of requests for reuse that are processed in accordance with the provisions of the aforementioned Article 10 (Procedure for processing requests for reuse).
c) Promote that the information is provided in the appropriate formats and is updated as far as possible.
d) Coordinate and encourage promotional, awareness and training activities.

In the context of the V Open Government Plan, which is in the final drafting phase, several administrations refer to the implementation of open data strategies and plans. The following is a brief summary of two of the most noteworthy:
•	Access and integration plan for high-value geospatial information of the Ministry of Transport and Sustainable Mobility through the National Geographic Information Centre (CNIG). It aims at the publication of high value datasets with a spatial component in compliance with FAIR principles, the creation of digital maps, topographic and postal address bases integrating information from various sources and the development of an API to facilitate the use of the geographic information generated. 
•	Plan to improve access to data from the Official Gazette of the Commercial Register of the Ministry of the Presidency, Justice and Relations with the Courts. It aims to improve public access to the information published in the bulletin, increasing transparency and facilitating the re-use of market information.
In addition to those referred to in the above-mentioned plan, an increasing number of municipalities are developing their own data strategies. The strategies implemented in recent months by the following local authorities should be highlighted:
•	In May 2024, the Town Council of Chiclana de la Frontera approved its municipal ordinance on Data Governance. This step was published in the Official Gazette of the Province of Cadiz, indicating the municipality's commitment to efficient and transparent data management. column6:
Are there any processes in place to assess if public sector bodies are charging for data above marginal cost? (please see directive (EU) 2019/1024 on open data and the reuse of public sector information).

For Explanation:
* If yes, please specify the process(es).
column13:
In accordance with the regulations in force in Spain, reflected in "Article 7. Fees" of the Law 37/2007 on open data and reuse of public sector information, the reuse of datasets will be free of charge.

See more: https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2007-19814#:~:text=Subir-,%5BBloque%2012%3A%20%23a7%5D,-Art%C3%ADculo%207.%20Tarifas

Each of the datasets published in the National Catalog has a comment and remarks field, through which, users can report whether public sector agencies are charging for data above the marginal cost. These possible anomalies are evaluated by the platform administrator team. If any transgression of the current law is identified, the administrator will contact the publishing agency and refer them to their obligation to comply with the current law. 

It is the regulatory framework itself that is the process in place to ensure that public sector agencies do not impose charges on data reuse above marginal costs.

Given the challenge in the coming months of the need for public administrations in Spain to implement DCAT-AP-ES in the publication of data, materials have been developed to facilitate its implementation. Specifically, it is available:
•	The Implementation Guide. See here: https://datosgobes.github.io/DCAT-AP-ES/,

Further materials to accompany its implementation are under development. These include an application guide, a podcast and training videos. See here: https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/dimension1_2025_evidencia_p26b.png
2024:
In addition to the above-mentioned actions to address the challenges identified, new actions are being implemented over the last 12 months. These include the following:
- Challenge 1. To foster inter-administrative collaboration to generate data exchanges and facilitate data openness, a report is being prepared which lists applications, platforms and services that are being used by some municipalities and whose use could be extended to others if they were to publish the necessary data in the same format. 
- Challenge 2. To incentivise the implementation of processes to improve the management, quality and governance of open data in the context of the overall data strategy of each administration, the DG Data is working on a RD for a data governance structure, as stated in the Artificial Intelligence Strategy, Initiative 5.3 Common data governance of the NSA: ‘It is necessary to address the regulation from a comprehensive legislative approach, developing a data governance model. Indeed, this regulatory drive for effective data governance in the NSA will include the overall design of a data-oriented organisational structure, with the new Directorate General for Data of the Secretary of State for Digitalisation and Artificial Intelligence as the backbone and enabler. "
- Challenge 3. With the aim of enabling public workers to develop the necessary knowledge and skills in open data, the results of a two-pronged collaborative work have been published. Firstly, define the roles of the professional responsible for open data, their technical and specific competencies, as well as their functions within the organisation: skills, leadership, collaboration with other departments, application of ethical aspects, among others. Secondly, an ambitious compilation has been developed in the form of a catalogue of training actions, with a wide variety of material for the dynamization and creation of specialised profiles in this area. See here: https://encuentrosdatosabiertos.es/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/Reto-2.pdf
- Challenge 4. In order to facilitate the secure and voluntary exchange of datasets held by public bodies over which third party rights concur, different safe rooms have been set up, i.e. virtual spaces that facilitate the request of such data from citizens. These include the following:
· INE: Access to microdata for scientific purposes (Application for recognition as a research entity, Application for access to data for research entity).
· Access to data linked to Social Security: Social Security Investigation Chambers
· Access to Banco de España data: Banco de España Data Laboratory (BeLab)
· Access to data from the Institute for Fiscal Studies (Statistics Area ief.es)
- Challenge 5. In order to encourage the implementation of processes to improve the management, quality and governance of open data in the context of the global data strategy of each administration, the DG Data is working on a RD for a data governance structure, as stated in the Artificial Intelligence Strategy, Initiative 5.3 Common data governance of the NSA: ‘It is necessary to address the regulation from a comprehensive legislative approach, developing a data governance model. Indeed, this regulatory drive for effective data governance in the NSA will include the overall design of a data-oriented organisational structure, with the new Directorate General for Data of the Secretary of State for Digitalisation and Artificial Intelligence as the backbone and enabler. "

column13:
At both national and regional level, support is provided to administrations in the publication of open data. 
At the national level, this service is available through the channels set up for this purpose: mail, telephone and virtual meetings. See here: https://datos.gob.es/es/asesoramiento-y-soporte 
The daily activity of the support service is recorded in a file that facilitates the monitoring of the actions carried out and is quantified and analysed by means of internal dashboards. As a result of these analyses, new actions are programmed, adjusted and reoriented. See here: https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/dimension1_2024_evidencia_p27.png 
At the regional level, regions such as Catalonia offer support services to local authorities in the publication of data. See here: https://formaciooberta.eapc.gencat.cat/espaistematics/gestio-dades/la-xarxa-de-governs-oberts-de-catalunya-paradigma-de-collaboracio-interadministrativa-i-suport-als-ens-locals.html
At the provincial level, several provincial councils provide legal, economic and technical assistance and cooperation to municipalities in the field of open data. Their impact is of particular importance in smaller municipalities, with less economic and management capacity, to which they provide services that they could not provide on their own. These include the Diputación de Barcelona, the Diputación de Castellón, the Diputación de Córdoba and the Diputación de Gipuzkoa Irekia. column13:
The functionalities for contributing datasets are the same as for any public sector publisher.

Most published datasets come from public sector entities. However, a group of researchers - Foundation for the Promotion of Health and Biomedical Research of the Valencian Community (FISABIO), listed as a private entity in the portal's faceted search engine- publishes a dataset of semantically enriched medical images from its research activities. 

https://datos.gob.es/es/catalogo?_publisher_display_name_limit=0&publisher_display_name=Fundaci%C3%B3n+para+el+Fomento+de+la+Investigaci%C3%B3n+Sanitaria+y+Biom%C3%A9dica+de+la+Comunitat+Valenciana+%28FISABIO%29

On the other hand and along the same line, another group -Mondragon University-contributes 94 datasets from a project on intelligent systems and IoT.

https://datos.gob.es/es/catalogo?_publisher_display_name_limit=0&publisher_display_name=Universidad+de+Mondrag%C3%B3n

It is expected that citizens or new entities from private sector will soon join with datasets of research projects, among others.
