column13:
2025:
The sustainability of the platform and the project is ensured thanks to the current agreement between the General State Administration and the public entity red.es, which is responsible for the management, enhancement, and maintenance of the portal. An even more ambitious agreement is currently being processed that will allow us to go much further in terms of open data at the national level. The agreement aims to promote the openness, reuse, and governance of public sector information, with a special focus on the State Public Sector, in coordination with the rest of the regional and local administrations in Spain, promoting the data economy and, in particular, the creation of new products and services, in collaboration with the private sector and civil society, for the benefit of society.
In the coming months, this four-year agreement will be published in the Official State Gazette. See here: https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/dimension1_2025_evidencia_p4.png
2024:
The national datos.gob.es catalogue is part of the actions that make up the Spanish government’s ‘Aporta’ initiative on open data. The national strategy is seen as a public policy with funds from the administration itself for its management and support.  This sustainability is based on the current agreement (C-003/19-ED) between the General State Administration, through the current Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation, and the public business entity Red.es to promote the opening and the re-use of public sector information. The duration of the Agreement extends until mayo de 2028,  See information here: https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/dimension1_2023_evidenciapregunta_17a.png

In addition to the dashboard mechanisms mentioned above, the portal has a backoffice that allows certain actions to be carried out by publishers to be monitored. These actions allow publishers to take action on the feedback they receive. The most relevant functionalities available are: 
- federation management console, through which publishers manage and schedule automatic data federation (harvesting) tasks. 
- check for broken links. This functionality allows publishers to see the results of the periodic broken link checks that the platform performs on the availability of the distributions published. 
- data availability, which makes it possible to manage data requests received by publishers, providing feedback to users and changing the status of each request based on the availability of new datasets. 
- comment management, to respond to comments on data sets received from users.

2024:
Dataset publishers can adjust the harvesting frequency (daily, weekly, biweekly, monthly), to ensure that high-frequency data is always up-to-date.
2023:
The NTI-RISP (technical standard compatible with the DCAT standard for the interoperability of data catalogues) establishes common conditions on the selection, identification, description, format, conditions of use and availability of the data sets produced or guarded by the public sector. These conditions are intended to facilitate and guarantee the re-use process, ensuring the persistence of information, the use of open formats, as well as the appropriate terms and conditions of use. Specifically, section III.5 of the NTI-RISP indicates that the information resources of periodic production or collection made available for re-use will be updated to their latest versions and the date of last update will be indicated, as well as the period of the update. 

In this sense, the initiative promotes the management of data sets published automatically and periodically via federation (harvesting). Through the federation console, publishers are informed when there has been a problem updating the metadata so that they can be corrected.

The quality of the metadata is checked at the time of registration and/or update of each dataset. Datasets that do not meet the quality standards established in the Spanish NTI-RISP compatible with DCAT are not allowed. The automatic federation mechanism or the manual upload method generates reports addressed to the publishers reporting when these quality standards are not met so that the metadata can be adjusted correctly. Changes are not saved to the dataset catalogue until they are successful. 
On the other hand, individualised audit processes are continuously carried out on publishers on the quality of metadata currently published on the portal. This audit follows the methodological approach of the Metadata Quality Assessment (MQA) proposed by the European Data Portal, evaluating the quality of metadata based on three complementary dimensions: discovery, interoperability and context. Likewise, as has been mentioned previously, distribution URLs are periodically evaluated to inform data managers of possible broken links. column13:
Currently, the Initiative promotes the use of standard licenses (such as CC BY) for the re-use of public sector information in Spain. However, our current legislation indicates that open data publishers may provide licenses for the re-use of documents, which must be available in digital format and be processable electronically. The conditions incorporated in the licenses must respect the following criteria:

a) They must be clear, fair and transparent.
b) They must not restrict the possibilities of reuse or limit competition.
c) They should not be discriminatory for comparable categories of re-use, including cross-border re-use.

These conditions are compatible with the CC-BY 4.0 license.

These conditions can be viewed at the following URL:
https://datos.gob.es/en/avisolegal
Royal Decree 24/2021: https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2021-17910
Royal Decree 1495/2011: https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BO

The Spanish specification for the interoperability of data catalogues, NTI-RISP, was defined in 2013 [https://www.boe.es/eli/es/res/2013/02/19/(4)/con] and is DCAT compliant. Do you have a definition of open data reuse in your country?
 
For Explanation:
* If yes, please specify it.
column13:
2025:
The definition included in Law 37/2007, detailed in the response from previous years, is still in force and is the basis for the various strategic documents and plans on which progress continues to be made. As an example, the forthcoming V Open Government Plan, where the "Reuse of Public Sector Information (RISP)" is defined in the wake of the Law: "Consists of the use, by natural or legal persons, of data generated and held by public sector bodies for commercial or non-commercial purposes. It consists of the use, by natural or legal persons, of data generated and held by public sector bodies for commercial or non-commercial purposes. This concept seeks to maximise the value of public information and data by allowing it to be copied, disseminated, modified, adapted, extracted, reordered and combined. Making public information available by public administrations increases administrative transparency by reinforcing democratic values and enabling citizen participation in public policies".
Other related definitions, such as the "Right of access to public information" or the "General Access Point to Public Administrations (PAG)" are also included in this plan.

2024:
2024:
The definition included in Law 37/2007, detailed in the previous year's response, is still in force, and work is being done to disseminate it and make it known to society as a whole. Between March and April 2024, a campaign has been carried out to bring this and other definitions related to open data closer to citizens. A series of gifs and an interactive infographic have been created and disseminated on social networks on concepts related to the subject.
•	Interactive infographic: https://datos.gob.es/en/documentacion/glossary-data-related-terms
•	Broadcast on Twitter: https://x.com/datosgob/status/1765775037053731207?s=20
•	Spread the word on LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7171519979584897025
2023:
The Law 37/2007 on public sector re-use defines the re-use of open data as a guarantee that must be ensured by all public administrations in Spain. The definition is as follows:  

"The re-use of public sector information consists of the use by natural or legal persons of information generated by public sector bodies, for commercial or non-commercial purposes. Re-use involves, by way of illustration, activities such as copying, disseminating, modifying, adapting, extracting, rearranging and combining the information".  

Following the incorporation of the provisions of the European Directive 2019/1024, Law 37/2007 includes a series of guidelines to ensure and encourage re-use: Offer data in machine-readable formats, with the highest level of accuracy, accessible, easy to find and locate, massively downloadable, in real time for dynamic data and published together with its metadata.  

In order to inform the public about the key changes to the Law, this summary infographic was produced last March 2023: https://datos.gob.es/en/blog/keys-law-re-use-public-sector-information-spain

With the upcoming launch of the new datos.gob.es platform, the automatic reporting created in Looker Studio and drawing from various monitoring tools such as Google Analytics 4 (GA4), Metricool, Hotjar, etc. is being enriched. For example, information on high-value data will be added (this issue is explained in question 4 below). These tools allow for real-time monitoring:
•	The number of users accessing the portal.
•	The most consulted pages and datasets.
•	User interaction, such as the use of different resources through resource downloads and other behavioural metrics such as engagement.
•	Trends in demand and re-use of published information.
Evidence:
•	https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/evidencia_impacto_1.1.jpg
•	https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/evidencia_impacto_1.2.jpg
•	https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/evidencia_impacto_1.3.jpg
Improvements have also been made to the Google dataset search engine. Technical improvements are being applied to the implementation of structured data markup (using the DCAT-AP standard and the Schema.org vocabulary), in order to facilitate the indexing and visibility of datasets in Google's Dataset Search. This action allows to obtain indirect metrics of traffic originating from search engines to specific sets.
In addition, work has begun on monitoring external reuse by extracting mentions, references and links to datasets from the GitHub platform. The analysis of these repositories allows:
•	Identify projects, applications or scripts that reuse data published in datos.gob.es.
•	Obtain qualitative metrics on the type of developments driven by open data.
•	Recognise patterns of re-use in the technical community, as well as key actors (users, organisations, thematic areas).

Link: https://github.com/datosgobes/DCAT-AP-ES/pulse

On the other hand, the monitoring of companies and enterprises continues. Between June 2024 and May 2025, 41 success stories have been added/updated. In order to identify new use cases, we have continued to focus on social media campaigns and active search.

•	Social media campaigns: https://x.com/datosgob/status/1810984812792177080 ; 
•	Personalised contact via email with more than 40 potential reusing companies, with whom telephone meetings have been held on request.
With regard to data communities, work has continued locating new working groups focused on data and potential reusers, such as Geochicas (https://elpais.com/america-futura/2025-03-10/los-mapas-creados-por-mujeres-que-desafian-el-poder-de-google-maps.html) , and collaboration has continued with those already identified.

Collaboration between open data initiatives is maintained, to achieve a cross-cutting view of what is being done not only by private re-users, but also by successful cases of open data re-use carried out by the administration itself. For example, from datos.gob.es we have had some contacts that have resulted in a series of podcasts:

•	Reuse of research data, with the Consortium of University Services of Catalonia (CSUC) and the Madroño Consortium. https://datos.gob.es/en/comunidad-risp/podcast-data-and-open-knowledge-spanish-institutions 
•	Promotion of open data competitions, with the Junta de Castilla y León and the Basque Government. https://datos.gob.es/en/comunidad-risp/podcast-data-contests-drive-reuse
•	Reuse of geospatial data, with the National Centre for Geographic Information (CNIG) and the Government of Aragon. https://datos.gob.es/en/comunidad-risp/podcast-high-value-data-geospatial-component 

These talks have allowed us to identify new success stories.

2024:
2024:
The process of monitoring the re-use of open data from the national open data initiative remains the same. However, it has been adapted to new technological developments in the platform linked to the project in order to track access to the datasets more comprehensively. Over the last year, Google Analytics 4 (GA4) has been implemented, which provides a more accurate measurement of these metrics. For example, to visualise the most popular datasets in real time, a customised and interactive report has been created in Data Studio. See here:
•	https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/evidencia_1/evidencia_1.1.png
•	https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/evidencia_1/evidencia_1.3.png
Monitoring of companies and applications has also continued. Between June 2023 and May 2024, some 40 success stories have been added/updated to the repositories of applications and companies in datos.gob.es. For the identification of new use cases, two paths have been followed:
•	Social media campaigns to encourage other reuse companies to share their experience with us: https://x.com/datosgob/status/1756941591950815650?s=20
•	Active search, through monitoring of social networks, web portals and media to identify projects likely to use open data. In total, more than 30 additional projects have been identified and contacted to learn more about their use of open data.
With regard to the data communities, work has continued on monitoring the stakeholders already identified, as well as on the active search for new interest groups. In this respect, focus has been put on developer groups such as PyData (ttps://pydata.org/) and research groups such as FISABIO(https://datos.gob.es/en/blog/relevance-open-data-medical-research-case-fisabio-foundation).
In addition, close contact is maintained with all public bodies at regional and local level that carry out their own monitoring of use cases, such as the Junta de Castilla y León (https://datosabiertos.jcyl.es/web/es/aplicaciones.html)or the Zaragoza City Council (https://www.zaragoza.es/sede/portal/datos-abiertos/). This makes it easier to cover the whole of Spain.
2023:
The national open data portal (datos.gob.es) contains more than 68,500 federated open datasets and analytics tools are used to monitor the number of visits and downloads.    

Analytics tools, such as Google Analytics, are used to monitor visits and downloads of the datasets in the National Open Data Catalogue. Various customised reports are used to monitor dataset visits, audience type, downloads, etc. See here: https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/dimension2_2023_evidencia_pregunta_30.png 

Since 2020, the entity that coordinates the national open data portal, Iniciativa Aporta, started monitoring sectoral communities in relation to open data to encourage their participation. Contact with communities of data re-users is a strategy to measure the impact of open data re-use in Spain.   

Some of the communities that have been contacted over the last year are the geographic data systems (GIS) communities https://datos.gob.es/en/noticia/4-examples-communities-related-geographic-data-and-gis-systems 

- Gis and Beers: http://www.gisandbeers.com/  

- Geovolunteers: https://geovoluntarios.org/  

- GIS Community: facebook.com/ComunidadSIG  

- Geo Developers: https://www.geodevelopers.org/  

On the other hand, users can register applications and companies that reuse open data, and once the information has been checked to corroborate that it is correct, it is included in the portal.  Communication with users can be done through: https://datos.gob.es/en/report

column6:
Are there any activities in place to encourage public bodies to monitor the reuse of their own published data (e.g. incentives or obligations in place for public bodies or civil servants of national government)?
 
For Explanation:
* If yes, please (1) briefly describe these activities/incentives and (2) provide the URLs to support the answer.
column13:
2025:
Together with the regulations mentioned in previous years (Law 37/2007, Standard Ordinance of the Spanish Federation of Municipalities and Provinces (FEMP) on Data Governance, etc.), it is worth highlighting the data platform project of the General State Administration, included in the Digitalisation Plan of the Public Administrations, whose measure 6 is aimed at the transparent management and exchange of data. The aim is to promote and evolve the concept of re-use of public sector information by citizens and companies, favouring the development of high added value services. Among other actions, a large corporate data warehouse of the General State Administration will be implemented, the objectives of which are:
•	To have quality data that is secure, complies with data protection rules and promotes transparency. 
•	Encourage innovation and experimentation in the use of data in government by developing a framework for action to implement data sharing and transfer models.
Link: https://administracionelectronica.gob.es/pae_Home/pae_Estrategias/Plan_Digitalizacion_AAPP/Medidas.html
In addition, work is being done on the V Open Government Plan, which includes a line of work related to the openness and reuse of public information data. Among other actions, the Ministry for Digital Transformation and the Civil Service has set the overall objective of generating a common governance framework for the reuse of data internally and externally.
datos.gob.es is working and will continue to work on the dissemination of this and other regulations. For example, a podcast was developed to disseminate the Standard Ordinance on Data Governance.  https://datos.gob.es/en/comunidad-risp/podcast-data-governance 
In addition to actions at the regulatory level, training actions are also being carried out to encourage the monitoring of data re-use. Some examples are:
•	The Diputació de Barcelona has launched a pilot target local authorities with 5,000 to 20,000 inhabitants. These bodies will receive specialised training in the field of data re-use and will be able to benefit from customised support in order to create and manage municipal indicators. https://governobert.diba.cat/node/2441 
•	The Regional Government of Castilla-La Mancha has carried out several training courses for public employees on Transparency and Open Data, including information on re-use: https://docm.jccm.es/docm/descargarArchivo.do?ruta=2025/02/24/pdf/2025_1332.pdf&tipo=rutaDocm. 

2024:
2024:
In addition to the general state regulations mentioned in last year's response (Law 37/2007), work has continued this year to expand the regulatory framework at both local and sectoral level that affects this need. 
To this end, the new Standard Ordinance of the Spanish Federation of Municipalities and Provinces (FEMP) on Data Governance, which has been developed by a multidisciplinary group of experts in the field, and which is offered to the more than 8,000 municipalities in Spain as a model to follow, underlines the importance of measuring usage and offers guidelines to promote the use and monitoring of open data held by municipalities and councils, taking into account their particular needs (https://datos.gob.es/en/blog/new-femp-model-ordinance-data-governance). Among other issues, the ordinance includes:

•	Article 5: Promoting data orientation in the local community. The local authority administration will promote interoperability and the use of data in the local community, and will develop training and dissemination actions to promote the data culture and knowledge of the regulations on transparency and re-use of public information.

•	Article 23: Where one or more data sets are used for the automated formation of administrative acts or other decisions, this fact shall be recorded in the Inventory of data sets and information sources, indicating the nature of those acts and decisions.
References to open data, its use and monitoring in sectoral laws are also included. For example, the Draft Law (PL) on Sustainable Mobility, is committed to a digital and innovative transport system in which open mobility data will play a key role (https://datos.gob.es/en/noticia/boosting-promotion-open-data-through-sustainable-mobility-bill). Among other issues, this law encourages research and the creation of new developments and businesses based on the data generated in the transport and mobility ecosystem. In addition, the Law promotes the creation of a sandbox or testing environment to serve as an incubator for innovative mobility projects. The outcome of the tests will allow the administration to monitor the situation and acquire learning by observing the market in a controlled environment controlled environment.

Likewise, Royal Decree-Law 6/2023, of 19 December, which approves urgent measures for the implementation of the Recovery, Transformation and Resilience Plan for the public service of justice, civil service, local government and patronage, in its chapter 6 linked to Open Data, regulates the Justice Administration Data Portal, which should provide citizens and professionals with processed and accurate information on the activity, workload and other relevant data of all judicial and prosecutorial bodies, services and offices in Spain, provided by the Justice systems in the terms defined by the State Technical Committee for e-Justice Administration.

According to the aforementioned Royal Decree, to this end, the National Judicial Statistics Commission will determine the judicial statistics information to be published on the Portal. Within this Portal there will be a section where the information will be considered as "open data" 

2023:
-> The current legislation in Spain states all public bodies have the duty to encourage the re-use of their data. Among others, Law 37/2007 requires each organisation to set up the Unit responsible for information, which is entrusted with different functions, including coordinating re-use activities and encouraging promotional, awareness-raising and training activities https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2007-19814#:~:text=Subir-,%5BBloque%2017%3A%20%23a1%2D2%5D,-Art%C3%ADculo%2010.bis 

->There is also an agreement between the General State Administration and the public business entity Red.es, valid until May 2027, aimed at promoting openness and reuse of information in the public sector. In this agreement, it is agreed that a general function of promoting the reuse of information in the state public sector will be exercised, developing, to this end, study actions around reusing open data. See more: https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/dimension1_2023_evidenciapregunta_17a.png 

->In the last year, work has been carried out on the preparation of different official documents aimed at further encouraging the reuse of open data from the administrations. Among others:  

- Open Data Strategy (in the process of being drafted): https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/dimension1_2023_evidenciapregunta_3.png 

- National Open Government Plan: a commitment to use open data in the fight against political corruption and the development of regulations. https://transparencia.gob.es/transparencia/dam/jcr:fbb7d024-51e5-42f5-a31b-d08780e94055/170123%20IV%20PLAN%20DE%20GOBIERNO%20ABIERTO_ACTUALIZACION_EN_def.pdf 

- Data Driven Government Manifesto (draft): https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/dimension2_2023_evidenciapregunta_32.png 

- UNE specifications on data governance, management and quality https://datos.gob.es/en/blog/une-specifications-government-management-and-data-quality (All three standards are free of charge upon registration). 

      - UNE Specification 0077:2023 Data Governance: https://tienda.aenor.com/norma-une-especificacion-une-0077-2023-n0071116 

      - UNE Specification 0078:2023 Data management: https://tienda.aenor.com/norma-une-especificacion-une-0078-2023-n0071117 

     - UNE 0079:2023 Specification UNE 0079:2023 Data quality management: https://tienda.aenor.com/norma-une-especificacion-une-0079-2023-n0071118

Does your country have processes in place to monitor and measure the level of reuse of high-value datasets ((EU) 2023/138)?
 
For Explanation:
* If yes, please specify how and highlight challenges if any. 
* If you are an EFTA or a candidate country to the EU, please select 'not applicable'.
column13:
2025:
In view of the launch of the new datos.gob.es platform, specific labels are being incorporated to identify high-value datasets, as established by Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/138, in the framework of Directive (EU) 2019/1024 on open data and the re-use of public sector information. This labelling allows:
•	Prioritise the monitoring of strategic clusters for the economy and society.
•	Facilitate analysis of user access and interaction with datasets that should be published as a priority and free of charge.
•	Provide transparency on compliance with legal obligations associated with high-value data.

Evidence: https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/dimension1_2025_evidencia_p2_5.png

This procedure is part of the process detailed in the document "Iniciativa Aporta. Implementation Strategy" and summarised in the article "Measuring the impact of open data":  https://datos.gob.es/en/blog/measuring-impact-open-data
It is worth noting that during 2024 several analyses were carried out to identify the high-value data available in Spain and to monitor its use, the progress of which was summarised in this article: https://datos.gob.es/en/blog/advances-high-value-data-spain. 
In addition, various public bodies are also conducting studies on the categories of high-value data that they apply to their daily business. This is the case of the Ministry of Transport and Sustainable Mobility, which refers to the impact of mobility data in this document: https://www.transportes.gob.es/recursos_mfom/comodin/recursos/07_igr_redes_de_transporte.pdf. 

2024:
So far, the process of monitoring the use of HVD is partly the same as the one followed to measure the degree of re-use of other open data. 
In particular, qualitative analyses are being carried out through the collection of use cases. This procedure is detailed in the document "Iniciativa Aporta. Implementation Strategy" and summarised in the article "Measuring the impact of open data":
https://datos.gob.es/en/blog/measuring-impact-open-data
In this line, and in relation to the HVDs linked to the INSPIRE directive, i.e. geospatial, earth observation and mobility, a dissemination campaign has been carried out on cases of re-use based on data related to these categories. Specifically, the catalogue of solutions housed in datos.gob.es has been enriched with numerous applications developed based on this type of data.
See here:
https://datos.gob.es/es/aplicaciones?search_api_views_fulltext=Centro+National+Information+Geogr%C3%B3n+Geogr%C3%A1fica+%28CNIG%29&search_submit=Search
These examples of re-use, aimed at reflecting the impact of this type of data, have been disseminated through a recently published note: https://datos.gob.es/es/blog/aplicaciones-de-datos-geograficos-abiertos-del-centro-nacional-de-informacion-geografica
In addition, studies are beginning to be carried out to measure the impact of these data categories. For example, in the case of geospatial data, the following reports have been produced:
•	Geospatial data in the Ministry of Transport and Sustainable Mobility. Impact of information co-produced by IGN and CNIG (2024). https://www.idee.es/resources/documentos/CNIG-ES_Cost_Benefit_Central_SDI_Node_v018.pdf
•	ICEARAGON and ARAGEA performance report by the Government of Aragon (2024), where it is estimated that these services have resulted in savings of almost two million euros for all Aragonese in 2023. https://www.aragon.es/documents/d/guest/informe_rendimiento_2023

The summary of both reports is available here: https://datos.gob.es/en/blog/what-value-open-geographic-data

In parallel to the collection of use cases linked to HVD, a series of analyses are being carried out to identify the high-value data available in Spain:

•	Statistical data:  https://ine.es/ss/Satellite?L=es_ES&c=INEmasNoticia_C&cid=1259954427449&idp=1254736092075&pagename=masINE%2FmasLayout ; https://datos.gob.es/en/blog/high-value-statistical-datasets-foreseen-national-statistical-plan-2021-2024 
•	Geospatial data: https://datos.gob.es/en/blog/complying-europe-inspire-and-high-value-geospatial-assemblies-regulation
•	Earth observation and environmental data: https://datos.gob.es/es/blog/cumpliendo-con-europa-el-reglamento-de-conjuntos-de-alto-valor-de-observacion-de-la-tierra-y
•	Content relating to the remaining high-value categories will be published soon, currently available here:
o	https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/evidencia_2/evidencia2.png
o	https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/evidencia_2/evidencia3.png

column6:
Has your government specified what 'impact of open data' means (e.g. in a strategy document)?
 
For Explanation:
* If yes, how do you define the impact of open data in your country? 
* If possible, please provide a URL to a public document describing it.
column13:
The Aporta Initiative, the Spanish government's current national strategy, has been working and developing actions under the premise that measuring the impact of open data must be done from both a qualitative and quantitative point of view (see more: https://datos.gob.es/en/blog/measuring-impact-open-data ). Currently, in the Initiative's implementation strategy, the following definition is included in the section "Definition and application of progress and impact indicators":  

Within the framework of the Aporta Initiative, impact is understood as: any positive effect or benefit obtained directly or indirectly for individuals, communities or society, which occurs over a certain period and which results from the development of different activities in each area characterised using open data to an end.   

Link to the strategy: https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/iniciativa_aporta_-_estrategiaejecucion_2021_v01.pdf (page 5)  

The new national open data strategy, which is currently under development, continues to underline the need to further specify and work on the definition of impact indicators for open data policies to evolve from more quantitative to more qualitative measures. See here:   

https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/dimension2_2023_evidenciapregunta_34.png

column6:
Do you have a methodology in place to measure the impact of open data in your country?
 
For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe the key points of this methodology.
column13:
2024:
During this year a new methodology proposal has been created to measure the impact of open data in Spain: https://encuentrosdatosabiertos.es/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/Reto-3-%E2%80%93-Metodologias-para-medir-el-impacto-del-dato.pdf. This reference document, developed by a multidisciplinary working group from different public administrations and universities, was presented during the III National Meeting on Open Data.
In addition, work has been carried out this year to refine the methodology outlined in the 2023 response. To this end, a report has been produced which analyses existing best practices for measuring the impact of open data in Europe, based on the Open Data Maturity Study 2022. The report provides a comparative analysis of the countries that have scored above 500 points in the Impact dimension, regardless of their overall score and position in the ranking. On this basis, it draws recommendations and good practices that aim to provide ideas on how to improve the impact of open data on each indicator. https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/doc/file/informe-buenas-practicas-en.pdf.
Agencies and foundations are also working to develop methodologies to measure the impact of data. For example, the COTEC Foundation's report, The Reuse of Open Data 2024, includes a section called "2.3. Methodology for studying the re-use of published data", which details the methodology followed. https://cotec.es/proyectos-cpt/la-reutilizacion-de-datos-abiertos-2024/
2023:
-> In the section "Definition and application of progress and impact indicators" from the document "Iniciativa Aporta. Implementation Strategy", is stated:   

Attention will be paid to the definition and regular maintenance of progress and impact indicators for the opening and re-use of public sector information. To this end, and being aware of the difficulty involved in measuring impact, we will work on the approach to impact measurement that we have been following from the open data and reuse of public information initiative of the Government of Spain and which is inspired by the recommendations provided by several guides that we consider to be of reference in this aspect: the UNE 178301:2015 standard, the framework of common methods for the evaluation of open data, the guide for the empirical analysis of government open data initiatives and the taxonomy of the impact of open data. (...)  

See more here: https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/iniciativa_aporta_-_estrategiaejecucion_2021_v01.pdf (page 5)  

The method used to measure this impact is based on the two main components mentioned above: a quantitative analysis through indicators on data publication and its characteristics, and a qualitative analysis through the collection of data use cases. More details here: https://datos.gob.es/en/blog/measuring-impact-open-data   

->In addition to this methodology, the Asociación Multisectorial de la Información (ASEDIE), which brings together the infomediary companies in our country, periodically develops reports on the impact of open data on public and private companies in Spain.  

https://datos.gob.es/en/noticia/11th-edition-asedies-infomediary-sector-report-available  

In order to measure the economic impact of the reuse of data, a methodology is developed that has proven to be effective year after year. See details in the Chapter 2 of the report: https://static1.squarespace.com/static/600a99c4d2a8133c3599fc67/t/6447cfd13b93713076afc842/1682427878064/Asedie+Report+2023+VF.pdf

Is there collaboration between government and civil society or academia to create open data impact in your country?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please provide an example
* If possible, URLs to such projects and collaborations.
column13:
2025:
In addition to the agreements mentioned in previous years, collaboration between civil society, academia and public bodies has continued to expand over the past year. Some examples are shown below:
•	Asedie (Multisectoral Information Association) and the Universidad Rey Juan Carlos (Madrid) have launched the Open Data Reuse Observatory to promote the reuse of open data. It already has the commitment of some public bodies such as:
o	 Madrid City Council (September 2024): https://opendatareuseobservatory.org/2024/11/el-ayuntamiento-de-madrid-es-pionero-al-adherirse-al-manifiesto-del-observatorio-open-reuse/ 
o	The National Geographic Institute (IGN) and the Autonomous Body of the National Centre for Geographic Information (CNIG), through the Ministry of Transport and Sustainable Mobility (February 2025): https://blog.idee.es/archivo/-/blogs/el-ign-y-el-o-a-cnig-se-adhieren-al-manifiesto-por-los-datos-abiertos-reutilizables-1#:~:text=Dicho%20Observatorio%20fue%20creado%20el%2026%20de%20febrero,promover%20la%20formaci%C3%B3n%20en%20el%20ecosistema%20de%20datos.

•	The Cabildo de Tenerife and the University of La Laguna have developed a Sustainable Mobility Strategy in the Macizo de Anaga Biosphere Reserve in order to obtain real-time data that will allow them to take measures adapted to demand: https://www.ull.es/portal/noticias/2024/el-cabildo-de-tenerife-y-la-ull-colaboran-en-un-estudio-de-movilidad-sostenible-para-el-macizo-de-anaga/. 
•	Valencia City Council has renewed two agreements with the University of Valencia to promote good governance in the city. It will promote the Chair in artificial intelligence and research in data analytics through a global grant of 60,000 euros. The aim is to promote the use of artificial intelligence techniques, information visualisation and web technologies applied to relations between citizens and the municipal government, transparency and the use of open data: https://www.valencia.es/cas/actualidad/-/content/convenios-universitat-val%C3%A8ncia-ayuntamiento-buen-gobierno-1. 
•	Valencia City Council also approved a grant of 70,000 euros to the Polytechnic University of Valencia (UPV) through the signing of a collaboration agreement for the creation of the Chair of City Governance, with the aim of promoting training, dissemination and research activities on transparency, open government and open data: https://www.valencia.es/cas/actualidad/-/content/convenios-universitat-val%C3%A8ncia-ayuntamiento-buen-gobierno-1 . 
•	The Community of Madrid collaborated with the King Juan Carlos University of Madrid in the celebration of DATAMAD 2024. The event included a workshop on how to reuse open data and a datathon: https://opendatareuseobservatory.org/2024/11/datamad-2024-generando-valor-con-los-datos-abiertos-de-la-comunidad-de-madrid/ . 

2024:
2024:
In addition to the agreements published during previous years, more agreements have been signed in recent months to promote openness and data sharing, as well as related capacity building. Some examples are:
•	The Government of Navarre signed an agreement with the Public University of Navarre (UPNA) to disseminate datasets on its structure, activity, economic data and staff: https://www.navarra.es/es/-/nota-prensa/el-portal-de-datos-abiertos-de-navarra-incorpora-informacion-aportada-por-la-upna-reutilizable-por-entidades-y-particulares

column6: Automated feedback mechanisms tracking users´ access to datasets
column13:
2025:
Most open data portals have automated analytics mechanisms. In the case of datos.gob.es, we provide further information on the procedure:
1 Quantitative data capture: Traffic is automatically tracked using tools such as Google Analytics 4 (GA4) and Google Search Console, which allow to record and segment data on:
•	Number of accesses to each dataset.
•	User source channel (organic, direct, referral, etc.).
•	Targeting by geographic location, device and browsing flow.
•	Search terms used by users to reach the portal from search engines.
This makes it possible to identify the most visited datasets and to understand the general access behaviour of different user profiles.
2 Tracking of user interaction: To understand how users interact with the datasets, specific elements have been configured in Google Tag Manager. This tool allows you to register customised events, such as:
•	Clicks on download buttons or links.
•	Choice of formats (CSV, JSON, XML, etc.).
•	Time spent in the dataset.
•	Interaction paths within the data tab.
The data collected is integrated into GA4, providing a detailed overview of the most consumed formats and conversion rates per resource.
3 Automated qualitative data collection: Solutions such as Hotjar and Microsoft Clarity are used to obtain automated qualitative information about the user experience. These tools generate:
•	Heat map by mouse clicks and mouse movements.
•	Logging of browsing sessions (anonymised).
•	Information on scroll depth, ignored areas and interaction patterns.
This qualitative analysis allows us to detect possible usability barriers and opportunities for improvement in the design of the dataset pages.
4 Real-time display: All the information obtained is integrated into an automated visualisation environment using Looker Studio, which allows:
•	Consult in real time the evolution of access to datasets.
•	Analysing consumer trends and behaviour.
•	Facilitate decision-making based on up-to-date and segmented data

2024:
Most open data portals have analytics mechanisms in place. In the case of datos.gob.es,automated tracking of user access to datasets is performed at several levels:
1.- Capture: quantitative data on users accessing the portal are analysed and interpreted, as well as the user's channel of origin, and the different segmentations by geographical location, devices used and the flows of pages accessed.
In addition, the queries made by the user to access the portal via search engines are analysed. The tools used are GA4 and Google Search Console. This analysis seeks to identify quantitative data patterns, most-consumed content and trends.
2.- Interaction: User interactions within the dataset are analysed. In order to know user interactions, interaction elements have been configured in the tag manager tool that transfers the data to the analytics tool. The configured elements provide us with information on user actions, the most consumed formats, interaction times and conversions.
3.- Qualitative data: Qualitative tools such as Hotjar or Clarity are used to automate the collection of data on user behaviour within a page. Data on scrolling, clicks and heat maps are also extracted for each page. Analysis of this data allows modifications to be made to optimise the user experience.
4.- Visualisation: the above points are transferred to an automated visualisation tool integrated with the above tools, which provides real-time data capture and interaction data, facilitating the understanding of the data. 
See information here:

column6: Social media sentiment analysis
column13:
2025:
•	Social networks are key to identifying the needs of the reuse community in Spain. At datos.gob.es we are constantly monitoring the response to each user who contacts us through any of the available channels: Twitter (X), LinkedIn, Instagram or e-mail. In this sense, we have opted for the use of social metrics and indicators that allow us to indirectly measure the degree of interest, interaction and user perception of the content and services offered.
The portal maintains a consolidated presence on social networks such as LinkedIn, X and Instagram, where news, dataset launches, use cases, events and other initiatives related to the open data ecosystem are shared.
Through these platforms, key indicators are continuously analysed, such as:
Number of followers and monthly growth.
Interaction rate and reach per publication.
Engagement level (comments, shares, likes).
Types of content best received by users.
Detection of emerging issues of interest linked to the use and re-use of data.

2024:
To analyse user sentiment, information is collected from social media variables such as mentions, comments, shares and likes. Such interactions help to understand how users feel about open data reuse utilities and publications. The information is collected, on the one hand, automatically through the Metricool tool that integrates all the sentiment variables of each social network. On the other hand, a manual analysis is carried out by classifying mentions and comments by category for further analysis.

Are there any public bodies in your country that have developed a systematic ways of classifying the gathered reuse cases?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please provide a brief explanation of the process: According to which categories are reuse cases classified (e.g. by policy field)?
column13:
2025:
The established and recommended model for categorising use cases remains the same: the Technical Standard for Interoperability of Reuse of Information Resources, with special emphasis on those datasets considered to be of high value. 
Further developments now focus on continuing to facilitate implementation by various bodies and easy identification of datasets by re-users. To this end, an iconography has been created to facilitate the identification and understanding of the datasets. This is an advantage in guiding navigation in terms of both accessibility and efficiency in the re-use of public information.
A specific icon has been established for each category, based on:
•	The taxonomy of primary sectors included in the Technical Interoperability Standard for Reuse of Information Resources.
•	The thematic categories proposed in Directive (EU) 2019/1024 of 20 June 2019 on open data and reuse of public sector information and defined in implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/138 of 21 December 2022 establishing a list of specific high-value datasets and modalities for publication and reuse.
The aim is for them to be used in the different open data platforms linked to the Spanish public administration. Below are some of the pages included in the iconography style guide.
Evidence: https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/datosgobes/evidencia_impacto_3.jpg 
2024:
2024:
Over the last year, the national catalogue of open data has been enriched following the classification of the TSI (Technical Standard for Interoperability).

At the regional level, many portals have developed strategies to classify use cases according to sectors as determined by NTI. Examples include the Andalusian open data portal (https://www.juntadeandalucia.es/datosabiertos/portal/) or the Canary Islands open data portal (https://datos.canarias.es/portal/impacto/aplicaciones/).

But the main progress we have identified this year has been at the local level, many city councils have started to identify and classify use cases of open data at the political level, as in Bilbao (https://www.bilbao.eus/opendata/es/aplicaciones) or the City Council of Malaga, which this year has opted for open data(https://datosabiertos.malaga.eu/).
2023:
The classification of use cases, as with datasets, is based on different criteria. In the case of the national platform, datos.gob.es, which brings together a large part of the applications published by other data portals, different criteria are followed. These are: 

- Categories/themes related to the documented solution. These categories are included in the Technical Interoperability Standard for Information Resource Reuse, which establishes the reference for the categories of datasets collected: https://datos.gob.es/sites/default/files/doc/file/boe-a-2013-2380.pdf 

- Platform for which the solution is developed 

- Publication date 

- Aspects covered by the application (tags)

This map is intended to provide information on wildlife that could affect air operations. In addition, it offers a flight route planning tool, which allows identifying areas with presence or concentration of fauna, which represent a risk for aviation. The map is based on data obtained from studies on wildlife and habitats, as well as animal collision risks, carried out by airport managers. It includes the main wildlife hotspots, especially birds, in and around airports; the species of greatest relevance to air operations; and information on their movements, where available.
It also includes the mapping of protected areas in Spain, provided by the Ministry for Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge, as well as data on landfills, dunghills, wetlands, among others, provided by the autonomous communities.

For the construction of the digital model, public data sources have been used, such as information on buildings from the General Directorate of Cadastre and the point cloud in LIDAR format published by the National Geographic Institute (IGN), as well as a base layer on hotel accommodation in Denia, whose information has been collected from the open data portal of the Valencian Community and verified by the Denia Town Council. This and other information makes it possible to segment tourist spending by areas and to know the areas with the highest concentration of national and international visitors, which translates into an x-ray of the areas with the most activity, a key piece of information for the destination that is used to make decisions. The analysis of traffic, origin and correlation of visitor increases in the city or its surroundings has great potential when it comes to forecasting public services and promoting areas close to tourist attractions, events, new activities or companies.

Malaga City Council has developed a tool to measure how much of the income from tourism is invested in education or health: the Management System for the transition to a sustainable and integrated tourism model in the territory (Sostur). It shows, for example, that for every 1,674 euros that came into the province from tourism, only one euro was invested in the SDGs.
•	Link: https://www.malagahoy.es/malaga/Desarrollan-herramienta-Malaga-turismo-educacion_0_1908409830.html

For example, Park4dis contributes to the Sustainable Development Goals: goal 10 by reducing inequalities affecting people with disabilities, goal 11 by promoting inclusive cities and accessible transport, and goal 17.
•	Link: https://datos.gob.es/en/documentacion/municipal-innovation-through-open-data-solutions-make-municipal-services-more

In 2023, 29% use open data sometimes or almost never, although 58% of respondents did not answer this question. In the case of 2021, 13.9% use them frequently or always, while in 2019 they were 31.7% and in 2017 22.2%.
With respect to the sector of activity, in the healthcare field 3.2% use open data on a daily basis and 9.7% frequently. However, no positive responses were obtained in the healthcare and social services fields.

To do so, the central node of the Spanish SDI (IDEE) was considered as the starting point, including the services and data co-produced among the partners of the National Cartographic System (nodes from ministries, autonomous regions, and local entities were not included in the study's scope). The transposition of the Open Data Directive was made by Legislative Decree 200/2021 [ https://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:decreto.legislativo:2021;200#:~:text=DECRETO%20LEGISLATIVO%208%20novembre%202021%2C%20n.%20200%20Attuazione,%2821G00213%29%20note%3A%20Entrata%20in%20vigore%20del%20provvedimento%3A%2015%2F12%2F2021] that has amended the Legislative Decree no. 36/2006 [ https://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:decreto.legislativo:2006-01-24;36!vig= ].

This document  aims at supporting public administrations and other subjects in the process of open data and reuse of public sector information through specific requirements and recommendations. Specifically, these indications concern formats, publication, metadata profiles, licences and pricing, re-use requests and search tools, all aspects regulated by the Directive and the Decree.  The document also includes indications on organisational aspects and data quality, albeit not binding as they are not regulated by the indicated rules. Finally the document foresees the adoption of a guidance document for high-value datasets.

The open data strategy is defined by different legislation and documents.

The Three-year Plan for Information Technology in Public Administration is the national strategic document for all Public Administrations that oversees the digital transformation of the country [https://www.agid.gov.it/sites/agid/files/2025-02/Piano_Triennale_2024-2026_Aggiornamento2025acc_0.pdf]. The Plan is an important document to promote the digital transformation of the country and, in particular, that one of the Italian Public Administration, through the declination of the strategy on digitization into operational indications, such as objectives and expected results, traceable to the administrative action of PAs. Within the Three-Year Plan, a specific chapter (Chapter 5) is dedicated to Data of the public administration. In line with the principles set out and in continuity with the actions started with the previous Plans, the latest update 2025 of the Three-Year Plan 2024-2026 of this  aims at ensuring greater effectiveness of administrative activity in all processes involving the use of data, both with reference to the sharing of data between public administrations for institutional purposes, and with reference to the re-use of data, for both commercial and non-commercial purposes, according to the open data paradigm. The chapter includes specific objectives, expected results and actions to achieve those objectives also in line with the arrangements of the Open Data Directive, the national transposition act and the Guidelines on open data introduced by the national legislation.
In addition, in the latest update 2025 the section dedicated to data also focuses jointly to artificial intelligence. 

The article 50-ter of the Digital Administration Code (CAD) [ https://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:decreto.legislativo:2005-03-07;82  ], with the aim of redesigning digital governance, speeding up the digitization of public services and simplifying relations between citizens and the public administration, among other provision, foreseen the adoption of a National Data Strategy, by subsequent decree of the President of the Council of Ministers. 
The aforementioned article of the CAD, among other things, is a strong boost to the availability and interoperability of data of public administrations and public service undertakings, as well as the consolidation of the API catalogue, within the National Digital Data Platform established by the abovementioned art. 50-ter itself.

Furthermore, in line with the provisions of the action plan for EU eGovernment 2016-2020 (COM (2016) 179 final, and new European interoperability framework (COM (2017) 134 final, particular attention is given to the need for better coordination between various data policies, in particular for the implementation of the INSPIRE directive in the context of eGoverment policies. 
On this basis, the Three Years Plan highlights that the spatial information follows the implementing rules of the INSPIRE directive with regard to data harmonization, data access services, interoperability models, etc., whereas it is necessary to follow the rules of the implementation of the Open Data directive for everything concerning the conditions for data re-use (licensing, pricing, etc.).

column13:
2025:
The Sixth OGP National Action Plan includes specific actions for the pubblication of open data where the civil society is fully engaged (see https://open.gov.it/governo-aperto/piano-nazionale/6nap#gli-obiettivi-e-gli-impegni-del-6nap).
To date, there are several civic portals designed by civil society (e.g. OpenPNRR by Openpolis), as well as active initiatives and associations that have tried to define monitoring indicators to analyse how public investments create value and contribute to improving the lives of citizens and communities from different perspectives (PNRR Civic Observatory, Monithon, Libenter, Libera), transforming data into useful information for advocacy towards the decision-maker. 
The aim is to expand alliances and strategic partnerships to strengthen the implementation of open government principles, promoting discussion and exchange of practices on: transparency, open data, anti-corruption, equity, civic space and digital transformation.
2024:
The Fifth OGP National Action Plan includes a specific action for the pubblication of open data (in open and machine-readable format) about the public tenders, where the civil society is fully engaged (see https://open.gov.it/sites/default/files/media/documents/2022-03/5nap-piano-azione-governo-aperto-italia.pdf).

RESPONSE TO THE REVIEWER
The action includes the following steps:
- reconnaissance of currently existing data sources that can complement that of ANAC (the anti-corruption authority) on public tenders to best cover the information needs of civil society;
- Integration of ANAC data with other data sources - e.g.: OpenCUP (that makes available data, in open format, on public investment decisions financed with national, community or regional public funds or private resources registered with the Unique Project Code), OpenCoesione (open government initiative on cohesion policies in Italy with the aim of promoting the effectiveness of interventions through the publication of data on funded projects and widespread civic participation.);  possibility of synergies with the "participation" action and civic debate. 
This action will be in charge of civil society organizations and aims to make the results of empowerment concrete: ANAC will play the role of the facilitator;
- collection of feedback, suggestions for improvement of data portals;
- Updating or extending the semantic content published;
- publication of APIs.

The action also includes the integration of data 
coming from civic monitoring (i.e. citizen-generated data) on projects receiving support from public resources. Civic monitoring means collecting data, evidence, information, news, interviewing actors involved in the design and implementation of interventions, visiting places and construction sites, fostering transparency and collaboration, and making proposals.

column6:
Does the national strategy/policy foster the discoverability of the aforementioned types of data from your country on data.europa.eu?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe how.
column13:
2025:
Target 2023 - Documentation in the national open data catalog of at least 300 dynamic datasets.
2024:
As both national catalogues (open data portal and catalogue for spatial data) are harvested by data.europa.eu, all data documented in those catalogues are also discoverable in data.europa.eu. Consequently, this affects also the aforementioned types of data, as, based on specific actions and requirements in the Three-Year Plan for ICT, PAs are required to document data in the mentioned catalogues.

The Legislative Decree No. 36/2006 (amended by the Legislative Decree No. 200/2021 transposing the Directive (UE) 2019/1024) includes a specific provision for documenting data falling within the scope of the Open Data Directive and the related transposing Decree (so also dynamic data, geospatial data, etc.), through metadata, in the aforementioned catalogues. 
Furthermore, the Guidelines for the implementation of the National Open Data Decree (transposing the Open Data Directive) explicitly mention the European portal data.europa.eu.

Finally, in case of geospatial data the creation and publication of metadata are mandatory based on specific law (art. 59 of the Digital Administration Code). In case of geospatial data also available as open data, metadata documented in the catalogue for spatial data are also made available in the open data portal through GeoDCAT-AP. In order to avoid duplications in data.europa.eu portal, a filter is applied to the endpoint for excluding metadata for spatial data (already harvested from the national catalogue for spatial data).

column6:
Does the national strategy/policy outline measures to support the reuse of open data by the public sector?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe the measures.
column13:
2025:
Target 2024 - Documentation in the national open data catalog of at least 400 dynamic datasets.
2024:
The Article 50 of the Digital Administration Code (CAD) [ http://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:decreto.legislativo:2005-03-07;82!vig= ] expressly states that the data of public administrations are formed, collected, stored, made available and accessible through the use of information and communication technologies that allow their use and re-use by other public administrations and by private (citizens, businesses …), in accordance with the conditions established by law.

The subsequent article 52 also provides, with reference to reuse by the public sector, that in the definition of the specifications or the outlines of the contracts, relating to products and services that involve the production, collection and management of data, the administrations provide for suitable clauses to allow the use, in accordance with the provisions of (aforementioned) art. 50.
Furthermore, the same article 52 provides that the activities aimed at ensuring the access and re-use of public administration data fall within the parameters for assessing managerial performance.
The same article 52, to support the re-use of open data by the public and private sector, establishes the principle “Open data by default”.

Moreover, in Italy, almost all Regions and many municipalities have their own “policy to support the reuse of open data”. [ https://www.dati.gov.it/riferimenti-normativi-linee-guida-regionali ] 
In general, these administrations proceed with the adoption of dedicated policies and local guidelines for the effective implementation of the national strategy on the territory.
In this regard, it should be noted that in order to harmonize the process of exploiting public data (at national, regional and local level) the strategy defined by the individual administrations has to comply with the strategy set out in the Three-Year Plan, resulting in disciplinary liability and economic damage in case of non-compliance (L. 208/2015, art.1, co 512-517).
[ http://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:legge:2015-12-28;208!vig= ]
The Three-Year Plan explicitly states that the enhancement of public information assets is a strategic objective for the Public Administration to effectively address the new challenges of the data economy also to provide policy makers with data-driven tools to be used in decision-making processes.
In this context, a National Digital Data Platform (PDND - Piattaforma Digitale Nazionale Dati) is established by the art. 50-ter of the mentioned Digital Administration Code that will enable public administrations to share its own data through APIs also with the aim to develop data-driven policies. The Plan includes specific actions for public administrations for the implementation of PDND.

Furthermore, the Legislative Decree No. 36/2006 (amended by the Legislative Decree No. 200/2021 transposing the Directive (UE) 2019/1024) ensures the application of the principle that documents and data shall be re-usable for commercial or non-commercial purposes.
2024:
The Article 50 of the Digital Administration Code (CAD) [ http://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:decreto.legislativo:2005-03-07;82!vig= ] expressly states that the data of public administrations are formed, collected, stored, made available and accessible through the use of information and communication technologies that allow their use and re-use by other public administrations and by private sector (citizens, businesses, ...) in accordance with the conditions established by law.
Furthermore, the Legislative Decree No. 36/2006 (amended by the Legislative Decree No. 200/2021 transposing the Directive (UE) 2019/1024) ensures the application of the principle that documents and data shall be re-usable for commercial or non-commercial purposes.
The Three-Year Plan for ICT in the PA 2022-2024 includes specific actions for smart communities related to specific project, such as the Smarter Italy project which intends to experiment with new technological solutions, alongside mechanisms of open innovation and smart procurement for the territories. Smarter Italy will initially operate on three lines: Smart mobility, Cultural heritage and Wellbeing, to gradually extend the digitization processes to the environment, infrastructures and training. The reuse of open data in this context is crucial.

Finally, the 2025 Strategy for Technological Innovation and digitisation of the Country includes 20 objectives among which "Data for the Cities of the Future" aimed at reusing data created by the operators fullfilling public services also by private sector to develop new services, new entrepreneurial activities, new innovative solutions (see https://assets.innovazione.gov.it/1610546390-midbook2025.pdf).

column6:
Does the national strategy/policy mandate carrying out and maintaining a data inventory by public bodies, whether at national or local level?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly specify.
column13:
The Legislative Decree No. 36/2006 (amended by the Legislative Decree No. 200/2021 transposing the Directive (UE) 2019/1024) includes a specific provision for documenting data falling within the scope of the Decree and Directive, through metadata, in the national catalogues, the open data portal https://dati.gov.it and the catalogue for spatial data https://geodati.gov.it .

Article 24-quater, par.  2, D.L. n. 90/2014, converted into Law no. 114/2014, obliges all Public Administrations and public undertakings to notify the Agency for Digital Italy of the databases they own. 
[ http://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:decreto.legge:2014-06-24;90!vig= ]
As a result of the implementation of this rule, those databases are now documented in a special repository into the national portal dati.gov.it [ https://www.dati.gov.it/base-dati-informazioni ].

In addition, Article 50 of the Digital Administration Code [ http://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:decreto.legislativo:2005-03-07;82!vig= ] requires administrations to proceed with the analysis of their own data, within the scope of their institutional tasks, also in combination with data held by other subjects, whereas “Legislative Decree no. 33/2013, Articles. 3 to 9-bis”  [ https://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:decreto.legislativo:2013-03-14;33!vig=2019-06-05 ] provides for explicit actions for administrations aimed at the inventory, publication, access and re-use of data by administrations.

Finally, article 53 of the Digital Administration Code  states that the public administrations shall publish the inventory of data and metadata, as well as the related databases owned and the rules governing the access and the reuse of such data and metadata.

column6:
Do these data inventories include the data collected by public bodies that cannot be published as open data (e.g. in relation to the EU Data Governance Act (EU) 2022/868)? 

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly specify.
column13:
2025:
The art. 53(1-bis) states that public administrations shall also publish the catalogue of data and metadata, as well as the relevant databases they hold, with the exception of the data in the Tax Registry.
2024:
The aforementioned legislation affects both open and not open data. 
As indicated in the answer to the previous question, the database catalogue https://www.dati.gov.it/base-dati-informazioni collects information about the databases of the Public Administrations on the basis of the aforementioned D. L. 90/2014. This catalogue, integrated into the dati.gov.it national portal, has been made available for query functions and is particularly relevant with a view to fostering the sharing of data between public administrations, for institutional purposes which, together with the re-use of open data, represents one of the policies for enhancing the value of public information assets. These resources cannot be published as open data.

column13:
The responsabilities are distributed among several public administrations.
The Agency for Digital Italy (AgID) is in charge of the execution of legislation provisions for open data, the implementation of the Open Data Directive according to the national open government policies. The Agency manages the national open data portal and the national catalogue for spatial data, defines national guidelines about the information of the public sector, defines the national metadata profiles. 

The Department for Digital Transformation is the support structure for the Minister for Technological Innovation and Digital Transition for the promotion and coordination of the Government's actions aimed at defining a unitary strategy in the field of digital transformation and modernization of the country through digital technologies.
The Department is in charge, inter alia, of the implementation of the APIs catalogue (and the linked National Digital Data Platform) and the repository of ontologies, schemas and controlled vocabularies for the semantic interoperability.

AgID and the Department for Digital Transformation jointly pursue the strategic objectives relating to the enhancement of the open data provided for in the Three-Year plan for ICT in the Public Administration.

The Open Government Partnership (OGP) is an international initiative that aims to obtain concrete commitments from governments in terms of promoting transparency, supporting civic participation, fighting corruption and spreading, within and outside the Public Administration, new technologies to support innovation.
The member countries, including Italy, have approved the Open Government Declaration, which commits them to undertake new initiatives in the field of open government. The OGP community is based on the inclusion and partecipation of various stakeholders; in Italy the OGP community includes 57 public administrations and 53 representatives from civil society.
One of the main themes that has always been the subject of attention is represented by the Open Data.

Other responsabilities lie with other public administrations, also at regional and local level.

At level of individual public administration, a relevant role in the organisation of offices and resources for the process of opening and reuse of data is played by the Office of the Digital Transition Manager (RTD) established by Article 17 of the CAD - Digital Administration Code, who is responsible for the transition to the digital operating mode and who reports directly to the political top management or, in its absence, to the administrative management of the administration. The digital transition manager (RTD) plays a role of reference of the political and/or administrative top management and is a transversal figure across the entire organisation in power to act on all the offices and areas of the administration, on the one hand, and as a point of contact with the Agency for Digital Italy and the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, on the other, for issues related to the digital transformation of public administrations

The Guidelines for the Implementation of Legislative Decree No. 36/2006 (as amended by Legislative Decree No. 200/2021 implementing Directive (EU) 2019/1024), (see https://www.agid.gov.it/sites/default/files/repository_files/lg-open-data_v.1.0_1.pdf)provides, inter alia, recommendations on roles and responsibilities for the open data process.  In paragraph 5.1.1. - Roles and responsibilities -  state that to implement the process, it is first necessary to define clear internal data governance with the identification of roles and related responsibilities, and to integrate its steps both vertically, with respect to already established internal processes, and horizontally with respect to the needs of different administrations.
An essential role in the organization of offices and resources for the process of opening and reuse of data is played by the Office of the Digital Transition Manager (RTD) established by Article 17 of the CAD, who is responsible for the transition to the digital mode of operation and who reports directly to the political leadership body or, in its absence, to the administrative body of the public administration. Circular No. 3 of October 1, 2018, of the Minister of Public Administration, in order to ensure the full operability of the Office of the RTD, recommends that in addition to the tasks expressly provided for, the act of assignment or appointment should also provide the power, among other things, to establish thematic groups for individual activities and/or fulfillments such as the process of opening and publishing data. In case this power is not assigned to the RTD, the establishment of the "thematic" group may be directly decided by the political or administrative top management. In any case, the RTD must still be involved given its role as a reference of the political and/or administrative top management and a transversal figure across the entire organization in power to act on all offices and areas of the entity, on the one hand, and as a point of contact with the Digital Italy Agency and the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, on the other, for issues related to the digital transformation of public administrations, as also reiterated in the aforementioned Circular No. 3/2018. In the Guidelines, the Recommendation 4 states: it is recommended that the Digital Transition Manager (RTD) be tasked with setting up a working group (led by a manager and involving thematic managers from all offices in the administration that produce data), dedicated to the open data process and the implementation of these Guidelines within the institutional organization. However, the RTD must be involved throughout the aforementioned process.The open data working group is considered in the Guidelines as a structure for governing the open data process, deferring to the organizational autonomy of each entity the provision of any other structures and figures, as well as the identification of the tasks to be assigned to them.

Improving metadata and data quality is one of the objective of the Three-Year Plan for ICT in the PA, that has defined some specific actions for achieving the expected results.
AGID promotes the implementation and the use of the standard ISO 25012 on data quality, ISO 25024 on data quality measurement, and UNI-TS 11725 "Guidelines for measuring data quality”. Increasing the quality of data is a specific goal of the ICT  Three Year Plan (2022-2024: https://www.agid.gov.it/sites/default/files/repository_files/piano_triennale_per_linformatica_nella_pa_2022-2024.pdf) and a specific section is dedicated in the national Guidelines (https://www.agid.gov.it/sites/default/files/repository_files/lg-open-data_v.1.0_1.pdf).
In addition, AGID has adopted a specific act aimed at improving data quality, see https://www.agid.gov.it/sites/default/files/repository_files/circolari/dt_cs_n.68_-_2013dig_-regole_tecniche_basi_dati_critiche_art_2bis_dl_179-2012_sito.pdf 
and the measurement of the data quality, see https://www.agid.gov.it/sites/default/files/repository_files/documenti_indirizzo/iso_25024_agid_misurazione_della_qualita_dei_dati.pdf.

The Guidelines for the implementation of the Legislative Decree no. 36/2006 (as amended by the Legislative Decree no. 200/2021, transposing the Open Data Directive) has been introduced by the mentioned Decree in order to support public administrations and other subjects in the process of open data and reuse of public sector information through specific requirements and recommendations. Specifically, these indications concern formats, publication, metadata profiles, licences and pricing, re-use requests and search tools, all aspects regulated by the Directive and the Decree.  The document also includes indications on organisational aspects and data quality, albeit not binding as they are not regulated by the indicated rules. See https://www.agid.gov.it/sites/default/files/repository_files/lg-open-data_v.1.0_1.pdf

The aforementioned Guidelines includes a specific requirement that states that open data shall be made available for reuse under the conditions of the Creative Commons BY 4.0 licence, the Creative Commons Public Domain Dedication (CC0) licence or any equivalent or less restrictive open licence. This is also aligned to the arrangements on licenses set out in the implementing HVD Regulation, although only affecting HVD.

column6:
Does the national portal offer a preview function for geospatial data?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please provide the URL to an example documenting this feature.
column13:
The open data portal is linked to the national catalogue for spatial data, that publishes both open data and data not yet available as open data. In case of open data, metadata is made available, through GeoDCAT-AP, also on the open data portal where the dataset is referenced by specific URI. This URI is resolved through the metadata page on the national catalogue for spatial data where a preview function, joined to query and search tools, is available also in accordance with the OGC standards. An integrated geoviewer is available at https://geodati.gov.it/geoportale/geoviewer/ . Please note that the page related to the metadata of spatial data in the national open data portal includes the URI of that dataset in the national catalogue for spatial data (having the structure https://geodati.gov.it/resource/id/{dataset-id}) that is resolved by the metadata page in that catalogue.
As an example:
https://dati.gov.it/view-dataset/dataset?id=regione-toscana-zone-di-protezione-art-14-legge-regionale-3-94 
 Through that URI, that dataset can be visualised in the geoviewer available in the catalogue for spatial data.

It is therefore institutionally guaranteed to be sustainable.

Do you have a definition of open data reuse in your country?

* If yes, please specify it.
column13:
The Italian legislation expressly provides for the definition of reuse of open data in the Digital Administration Code - legislative decree 82/2005 - Article 1, paragraph n-bis), where reuse means "use of the data referred to in Article 2(1)(e) of legislative decree no. 36 of 24 January 2006";
 [ https://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:decreto.legislativo:2005-03-07;82 ]
The provision refers back to the definition contained in turn in Legislative Decree 36/2006 on the transposition of the PSI Directive, as subsequently amended by  the Legislative Decree 200 of 8 November 2021 transposing the Open Data Directive. Specifically:
(e) re-use: the use by natural or legal persons of documents held by: 
      (1) public administrations or bodies governed by public law for commercial purposes or for non-commercial purposes other than the institutional purposes for which the documents were produced, with the exception of except for the exchange of documents between public administrations or bodies governed by public law, or between administrations and bodies governed by public law, carried out exclusively within the framework of the performance of the institutional tasks of which they are holders; 
      (2) public undertakings and private undertakings referred to in Article 1, paragraph 2-quater, for commercial purposes or for non-commercial purposes other than those relating to the provision of services of general interest general interest services for which the documents have been produced, with the exception of for the exchange of documents between public undertakings and public administrations or bodies governed by public law set up exclusively within the framework of the performance of the tasks institutional tasks of the public administrations 
 [ https://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:decreto.legislativo:2006-01-24;36~art2-com1-lete  ]

Is there collaboration between government and civil society or academia to create open data impact in your country?
